I use about the same amount and the result is still very good.Smoked paprika: The smoky depth in this spice mix comes primarily from the smoked paprika. The difference between good quality smoked paprika and generic paprika is significant, so it’s worth buying a decent one. Spanish pimentón de la Vera is the benchmark if you can find it. It comes in sweet, bittersweet and hot varieties. I use the sweet smoked version here so the heat comes only from the chilli powder and jalapeño.EquipmentChopping boardChef’s knifeLarge heavy-based frying panMedium bowl (for the spice mix)Large bowl (for marinating the chicken)Serving tray
66c1f192153208554f46cde1aec1d039725f8079.author: Andy
66c1f192153208554f46cde1aec1d039725f8079.ingredients:
3 tsp chilli powder
1.5 tsp ground cumin
1.5 tsp smoked paprika
½ tsp garlic powder
½ tsp onion powder
¼ tsp dried mexican oregano
¼ tsp ground coriander
¼ tsp sea salt
¼ tsp ground black pepper
600g chicken thighs, thinly sliced
sea salt
juice of 1 lime
2 tbsp peanut oil (or other neutral oil)
1 white onion, sliced
1 red capsicum (bell pepper), sliced
1 green capsicum (bell pepper), sliced
1 Jalapeno chilli, finely chopped
6 cloves garlic, chopped
8 flour tortillas, toasted
lime wedges and salsa verde, to serve
coriander leaves, to garnish
66c1f192153208554f46cde1aec1d039725f8079.instructions:
Combine all the spices for the Mexican spice mix in a medium bowl and mix well. Set aside.
Place the chicken in a large bowl. Mix in the spice mix, pinch of salt, lime juice and half the oil until well combined. Set aside.
Heat the remaining oil in a large heavy based frying pan over high heat. Add the capsicums, onion, garlic and chilli and cook, tossing for 3-4 minutes, until starting to soften. Transfer to a bowl.
Add the chicken to the pan and cook for 6-8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through.
Return the vegetables to the pan and toss together for a minute or until heated through.
Transfer the chicken filling to a heated serving tray and serve with toasted tortillas, lime wedges, salsa verde and coriander leaves to garnish.

69648ac339a413b77ddd600aab36eddf9265f339.title: Summer Tomato Tuna Salad
69648ac339a413b77ddd600aab36eddf9265f339.text: Think of this as the protein-packed version of the bottom of a Greek salad, where all the dressing gets super concentrated, the vegetables are nicely marinated, and everything is fresh and juicy and good. For a quick summer lunch that's savory, punchy and filling, this hits the spot every time.
69648ac339a413b77ddd600aab36eddf9265f339.author: Justine Doiron
69648ac339a413b77ddd600aab36eddf9265f339.ingredients:
1 medium (5 oz) tomato
1/4 cup fresh dill
2 mint sprigs
1/4 medium sweet white onion
1/4 cup kalamata olives
2 tablespoons red wine vinegar
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 teaspoon Diamond Crystal kosher salt
1/2 teaspoon sugar
1/2 teaspoon freshly cracked black pepper
2 large eggs
1 (3 oz) can tuna (packed in oil)
2 large bread slices (toasted, for serving)
69648ac339a413b77ddd600aab36eddf9265f339.instructions:
Dice the tomato, finely chop 1/4 cup of dill and 2 sprigs of mint leaves (remove the stems), thinly slice 1/4 of a white onion and 1/4 cup of kalamata olives. Add all of this to a large bowl.
Drizzle in 2 tablespoons of red wine vinegar and 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil. Season with 1/2 teaspoon each of salt, sugar, and black pepper. Mix to combine.
Let all of this mingle together while you boil 2 eggs for 7 minutes. Shock them in an ice bath, then peel and quarter them. Add them to the bowl. Drain the tuna and add it in as well. Give it all a good mix.
Serve with big pieces of crusty toasted bread to soak up all the juices.

8a6a1ed6a1a524b66fe73754d3b5f2208eb3a07a.title: Basque Cheesecake (Creamiest Ever)
8a6a1ed6a1a524b66fe73754d3b5f2208eb3a07a.author: Joshua Weissman
8a6a1ed6a1a524b66fe73754d3b5f2208eb3a07a.ingredients:
8 large eggs
1 large egg yolk
2 lbs (908g) cream cheese, softened to room temperature
½ lb (227g) mascarpone, softened to room temperature
1.5 cups (300g) granulated sugar
2 tsp (8g) fine sea salt
2 vanilla bean pods, split and scraped, *see Notes*
2 cups (480mL) heavy cream
3 Tbsp (30g) cornstarch
Cooking spray, for greasing
Alternatively, you can use 1 Tbsp (15g) of vanilla bean paste, or 1 Tbsp (15mL) of vanilla extract.
8a6a1ed6a1a524b66fe73754d3b5f2208eb3a07a.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 450°F (232°C). Crack the eggs and egg yolk into a medium-sized bowl.
In a large-sized mixing bowl, use an electric hand mixer to beat the cream cheese and mascarpone on high speed until smooth, creamy, and slightly lighter in texture. Gradually add the sugar while mixing, then mix in the salt.
Add the eggs and egg yolks one at a time, scraping down the sides of the bowl as needed. Add the vanilla bean seeds, heavy cream, and cornstarch, then mix until fully incorporated.
Lightly spray the base of a 9” (23 cm) springform pan then place a full sheet of parchment over the entire base. Clamp the walls of the springform pan over the parchment lined base. Trim any excess with scissors. Cut a second sheet of parchment in half lengthwise. Lightly spray the sides of the pan then overlap the two halves of parchment to cover the sides. Trim the excess to 1” (2.5cm) above the top rim.
Transfer the batter to the prepared pan, optionally straining for a smoother texture. Tap the pan firmly on the counter to release any air bubbles.
Place onto the middle rack of the oven and bake for 12 minutes, rotate the pan 180°, then bake for another 12 minutes. Then lower the oven temperature to 325°F (163°C) and continue baking until the interior reaches 140°F (60°C) for a velvety, gooey center, about 25 minutes. The cheesecake will continue to cook from carryover heat and should reach at least 160°F (71°C).
Let the cheesecake cool at room temperature until it is no longer warm to the touch, then transfer it to the fridge for a minimum of 4 hours, or ideally overnight. Let the cheesecake sit at room temperature for at least 1 hour before removing it from the springform pan, slicing, and enjoying!

8b81f64fd16afc3c77eea1018ab2dad2e1798e70.title: The Perfect Cheesy Chicken Parmesan Recipe
8b81f64fd16afc3c77eea1018ab2dad2e1798e70.author: Joshua Weissman
categories: The Perfect Cheesy Chicken Parmesan Recipe
8b81f64fd16afc3c77eea1018ab2dad2e1798e70.ingredients:
2 lbs (908g) boneless skinless chicken breasts, sliced in half horizontally
1 qt (950mL) water
2 Tbsp (20g) kosher salt
1 lemon, sliced into ¼” (6mm) rounds
4 cloves garlic, lightly bruised
1 tsp (2g) red pepper flakes
2 tsp (7g) whole black peppercorns
2 sprigs fresh rosemary
3 oz (85g) guanciale, or bacon, cut into ¼” (6mm) cubes
2½ Tbsp (40mL) extra-virgin olive oil
5 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
¼ cup (60g) gochujang
Small pinch of granulated sugar
1 tsp (2g) red pepper flakes
Kosher salt, to taste
1 (28 oz/794g) can crushed San Marzano tomatoes
½ bunch fresh thyme
2 cups (300g) all-purpose flour
4 large eggs
2 Tbsp (30mL) water
2 tsp (7g) kosher salt
1 tsp (3g) freshly cracked black pepper
2 cups (300g) panko breadcrumbs
Neutral oil, for frying (canola, avocado, etc.)
1 bunch fresh rosemary
2 cups (200g) low-moisture part-skim mozzarella, shredded
2 cups (200g) full-fat mozzarella, shredded
½ cup (50g) Pecorino Romano, shredded
Fresh chives, thinly sliced, *optional
8b81f64fd16afc3c77eea1018ab2dad2e1798e70.instructions:
Place each chicken cutlet between two sheets of plastic wrap or parchment paper. Using a meat mallet or rolling pin, pound the chicken to an even ⅓” (8mm) thickness.
In a large bowl, whisk together the water and salt until the salt is completely dissolved. Add the lemon, garlic, red pepper flakes, black peppercorns, and rosemary. Add the chicken, making sure the cutlets are fully submerged. Cover and refrigerate for 3–4 hours.
In a medium saucepan over medium heat, add the guanciale and olive oil. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the guanciale is golden brown and crisp and the fat has rendered, about 5–8 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the guanciale to a bowl or tray, leaving the rendered fat and oil in the saucepan.
Add the garlic to the rendered fat and cook, stirring often, until softened and lightly golden, about 1–2 minutes.
Add the gochujang and cook, stirring constantly, until it darkens slightly, begins to caramelize, and becomes fragrant, about 1–2 minutes.
Add the sugar and red pepper flakes, then pour in the crushed tomatoes and stir to combine. Season lightly with salt, keeping in mind that the guanciale and Pecorino Romano will add additional salt later.
Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Tie the thyme together with kitchen twine, if desired, and add it to the sauce. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has slightly thickened and coats the back of a spoon, about 15–20 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely chop the reserved crispy guanciale by hand or pulse it briefly in a food processor. Once the sauce has thickened, remove and discard the thyme. Fold in the chopped guanciale, adjust the seasoning to taste, and keep warm over low heat until ready to assemble.
Remove the chicken from the brine and discard the brine and aromatics. Rinse the cutlets briefly under cold water, then thoroughly pat dry with paper towels.
Set up a breading station with three shallow bowls or ¼ sheet trays. Add the flour to the first. In the second, whisk together the eggs, water, salt, and black pepper until smooth. Add the panko to the third.
Working one at a time, dredge each cutlet in the flour, shaking off any excess. Dip into the egg mixture, allowing the excess to drip away, then thoroughly coat in the panko, gently pressing the breadcrumbs onto the chicken to ensure an even coating. Transfer to a wire rack or sheet tray and repeat with the remaining chicken.
Fill a large cast-iron skillet with about 1” (2.5cm) of neutral oil and heat to 350°F (177°C). Working in batches to avoid overcrowding the pan, carefully lower the breaded cutlets into the hot oil. Fry until golden brown and crisp on the first side, about 2–3 minutes. Add a sprig of rosemary to the oil during the final 30–60 seconds before flipping.
Flip the chicken and continue frying until deeply golden and the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C), about 2–3 minutes more. Transfer the chicken to a wire rack set over a sheet tray and season lightly with salt while hot. Transfer the fried rosemary to the rack as well. Allow the oil to return to 350°F (177°C) before frying the remaining cutlets.
Preheat the broiler to high with a rack positioned about 6” (15cm) below the heating element.
In a large bowl, combine the low-moisture mozzarella, full-fat mozzarella, and Pecorino Romano. Gently toss until evenly combined.
Transfer the fried cutlets to a foil-lined baking sheet. Top each cutlet with about 4 oz (120g) of sauce, followed by a generous handful of the cheese mixture. Broil until the cheese is completely melted, bubbling, and beginning to brown in spots, about 2–4 minutes. Watch closely to prevent burning.
Transfer the chicken to serving plates. Garnish with thinly sliced chives, if desired. Serve immediately and enjoy!

3e5234c9f78bc635f7546bc43c13d4779b12f2f8.title: Curried Sausages
3e5234c9f78bc635f7546bc43c13d4779b12f2f8.text: This is a nostalgic dish for me. Mum would make this during the winter months and it was always a hearty and comforting dinner. It's basically pork sausages in a curry sauce that's served over rice. Now, I'v tweaked the recipe over the years so it's a little different to the once I grew up with. It still has the same main ingredients but we're using a Japanese curry sauce. You can make a curry sauce from scratch but using a curry cube is a great shortcut and I think it tastes just as good. Ingredient NotesJapanese curry cubes: A ready-made roux and spice blend in cube form. They dissolve into the cooking liquid to give a thick, glossy, mildly spiced sauce without having to build a spice blend from scratch. I use the S&B Golden Curry Sauce Mix. The medium heat level works well here, but mild or hot also work depending on your preference. Find it at Asian grocery stores or major supermarkets in the Asian aisle. Thick pork sausages: Thickness matters. Thin sausages will overcook and fall apart during the simmering time. Thick, butcher-style pork sausages hold their shape and stay juicy through the full cook. Beef sausages work just as well if you prefer. Whatever you use, leave them whole through the entire cook and cut them at the table or just before serving.Green apples: Two whole apples sounds like a lot, but they mostly break down during the final simmer and integrate into the sauce rather than sitting as distinct chunks. They contribute sweetness and a mild acidity that balances the richness of the Japanese curry. Green apples are better here than red; they’re less sweet, hold their shape a fraction longer, and their sharpness does more work against the fat in the sauce.EquipmentHeavy-based frying pan or wide saucepanWooden spoonChef’s knife and chopping boardKitchen scales
3e5234c9f78bc635f7546bc43c13d4779b12f2f8.author: Andy
3e5234c9f78bc635f7546bc43c13d4779b12f2f8.ingredients:
tbsp neutral oil (vegetable, canola, peanut)
8 thick pork sausages
sea salt and cracked pepper, to taste
1 brown onion, chopped
3 garlic cloves, chopped
1 carrot, peeled, chopped
2 green apples, cored, chopped large chunks
2 cups (500ml) water
92g Japanese curry stock cubes
Steamed rice, to serve
3e5234c9f78bc635f7546bc43c13d4779b12f2f8.instructions:
Heat oil in a heavy based frying pan on medium-high.
Cook sausages for 5 minutes, turning, until browned all over.
Add onion and garlic, cook for 3 minutes, until starting to soften.
Add carrots and cook for a further 2 minutes, stirring.
Stir in water and stock cubes, bring to a simmer, stirring to dissolve stock.
Simmer for 5 minutes and check for seasoning. Add salt and pepper if needed.
Add apples, stir to combine and continue simmering for a further 5 minutes.
Serve curry on steamed rice.

f813d1e5b67ae1563ae4a6b066a789aa45d90e89.title: Spicy Sausage and Chickpea Stew
f813d1e5b67ae1563ae4a6b066a789aa45d90e89.text: When Katelyn and I were living in Melbourne, this stew was on regular rotation during the colder months. It was perfect for those (many) grey Melbourne nights where you’re craving something hearty. It’s the kind of meal that feels like far more effort than it actually is.So, if you need a quick midweek meal and have some canned chickpeas in the cupboard, this is the one. A fast, one-pan stew made with spicy sausages, chickpeas, and tomatoes, inspired by Spanish cocido and ready in under 15 minutes. It’s bold, hearty, and ideal for busy weeknights. Packed with protein and finished with baby spinach, this stew is simple, satisfying, and has a little bit of heat.Everything comes together in one pan, which means minimal washing up at the end of a long day. The sausages bring all the flavour you need, the chickpeas add real body, and the tomatoes pull it all together into a proper sauce. We made this one on repeat and it never got old.Ingredient NotesSpicy pork sausages: These are the hero of the dish, so choosing a good one really matters. I went with a spicy Italian pork sausage, but Merguez or smoky chorizo both work beautifully here. Look for fresh sausages with good fat content rather than pre-cooked ones. Your local Italian deli or a quality butcher is the best place to find a great variety.Long red chilli: Adds heat and a fresh bite to the dish. If you want to dial back the heat, remove the seeds before slicing. If you love heat, leave them in or add a second chilli.Canned whole tomatoes: I prefer whole tomatoes over diced here because they break down more naturally as they cook and tend to have better flavour. Give them a rough crush with your spoon as they go into the pan.Canned chickpeas: Make sure to rinse and drain them well before adding to the pan. This removes the tinny flavour from the canning liquid and helps them absorb the sauce as the stew cooks.Equipment you’ll needHeavy-based frying pan with a lidChopping board and knifeCan openerWooden spoon or spatula
f813d1e5b67ae1563ae4a6b066a789aa45d90e89.author: Andy
f813d1e5b67ae1563ae4a6b066a789aa45d90e89.ingredients:
1 red onion
2 cloves garlic
1 long red chilli
4 spicy pork sausages
1 tbsp olive oil
sea salt, to season
1 tsp ground cumin
400g can whole tomatoes
400g can chickpeas, rinsed and drained
60g baby spinach
f813d1e5b67ae1563ae4a6b066a789aa45d90e89.instructions:
Dice the red onion, finely dice the garlic and thinly slice the chilli.
Pull the sausages from the casings and break up into thumbsized pieces.
Heat the oil in a heavy based frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the onion, garlic and chilli and saute for 1 minute.
Season with salt and cumin, then stir in the sausage pieces. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the tomatoes, then fill the can halfway with water and add to the pan. Stir in the chickpeas, cover with a lid and cook for 4 minutes.
Remove the lid and top with the spinach. Gently stir through until just wilted, then serve.

3351da5e57c893c8b1fa8e881a13478f3a976772.title: Tuna Melt
3351da5e57c893c8b1fa8e881a13478f3a976772.text: A proper tuna melt hits the spot! Crispy, cheesy, and packed with punchy flavour. This one’s loaded with capers, celery, lemon and a kick of Tabasco, all folded through flaky tuna. Pressed in golden sourdough with plenty of mozzarella and a sharp hit of pickled onion, it’s the kind of sandwich that makes toasties look weak. Serve it hot, serve it crunchy, and don’t skip the pickles on the side.
3351da5e57c893c8b1fa8e881a13478f3a976772.author: Andy
3351da5e57c893c8b1fa8e881a13478f3a976772.ingredients:
1 stick celery, finely chopped
2 tsp baby capers, drained, chopped
2 tsp dijon mustard
¼ cup mayonnaise
few dashes tabasco sauce
sea salt and pepper, to season
zest and juice of ½ lemon
200g canned tuna, drained
2 thick slices sourdough bread
1 cup grated mozzarella cheese
pickled red onion
30g butter
baby cornichons or dill pickles, to serve
3351da5e57c893c8b1fa8e881a13478f3a976772.instructions:
Combine celery, capers, mustard, mayonnaise, tabasco, lemon juice and zest in a medium bowl. Stir well then fold in tuna. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Place the tuna mix on 1 slice of the bread, then top with cheese and red onion. Sandwich together with another slice.
Heat a large frying pan over medium heat and add half the butter to melt. Transfer sandwich to pan and press down top with a protein press. Cook for 10 mins, until deep golden brown on the first side.
Add remaining butter to the pan and turn the sandwich over, press down again with a protein press or heavy cast iron pan.
Increase heat to medium-high and cook until the cheese has melted.
Slice the sandwich in half and serve with cornichons or pickles.

84e0e93d35155f93c91b5e1a486962323a928907.title: Ketchup
84e0e93d35155f93c91b5e1a486962323a928907.text: Have you tried to make ketchup (tomato sauce) at home before? You should! Give this recipe a try and see if you prefer to the store bought versions.
84e0e93d35155f93c91b5e1a486962323a928907.author: Andy
84e0e93d35155f93c91b5e1a486962323a928907.ingredients:
10 plum tomatoes, diced
2 small apples, diced
10 dates
150ml (5.3 fl oz) white vinegar
100g (3.5 oz) honey
200ml (6.8 fl oz) water
salt to taste
1 tbsp onion powder
1 tbsp garlic powder
1 tsp celery salt
1.5 tsp mustard powder
½ tsp allspice
½ tsp ground white pepper
84e0e93d35155f93c91b5e1a486962323a928907.instructions:
Add the diced tomatoes, diced apples, dates, white vinegar, honey, and water to a pressure cooker. Set the pressure to medium, and once it starts whistling, cook for 10 minutes. If you don’t have a pressure cooker, you can cook this in a pot over medium heat, which will take about 45-50 minutes. Stir every 5-10 minutes.
Once cooked, season the base of the tomato sauce with a pinch of salt, onion powder, garlic powder, celery salt, mustard powder, allspice, and ground white pepper. Mix well, then place everything in a blender and blend until smooth. Once blended, return the mixture to a clean pot.
Slowly reduce the sauce on medium-low heat for 1.5-2 hours until it reaches your desired thickness. The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon, and when you run your finger through it, the sauce should not flow back together.
This is your last chance to adjust the seasoning, so ensure it has enough salt. Pour the sauce into clean bottles, and once cooled, store them in the fridge for up to a month.

47826753bd1e091a50ecb431ec08d6358d4bae8f.title: Peanut Butter Pork Noodles
47826753bd1e091a50ecb431ec08d6358d4bae8f.text: What do I cook when Katelyn’s out and it’s just me at home? Noddles! Here is my new go-to quick noodle dinner with pork mince and peanut butter. It takes 25 minutes from start to finish and it’s very easy to make. We’re going to sear the pork mince and make sure we get some good colour on it, then use the peanut butter as the base for our sauce with soy, rice vinegar and lime juice. We’ll toss it through soft udon noodles and finish with chilli crisp on top. It’s rich, salty, sour and spicy. Ingredient NotesPeanut butter: For this recipe I used smooth peanut butter because the pork mince and chilli crisp offer so much texture, I wanted a velvety smooth sauce to complement the noodles. If you don’t have peanut butter, you can substitute it with any other nut butter you can find like almond or hazelnut. Just note that peanut butter gives you the best flavour for this dish. Udon noodles: I love udon noodles as they’re thick, chewy and smooth. The fresh vacuum-packed noodles take about 1-3 minutes to cook and dried udon takes 9-10 minutes. If you can’t find udon, use ramen or hokkien noodles. Soy sauce: I use a good chinese-style light soy sauce for this one. I wouldn’t recommend a dark soy as it will overwhelm the dish. If that’s all you have, use half the amount. EquipmentMedium pot (for boiling noodles)Medium saucier (for the sauce)Chopping boardChef's knifeTongs
47826753bd1e091a50ecb431ec08d6358d4bae8f.author: Andy
47826753bd1e091a50ecb431ec08d6358d4bae8f.ingredients:
1 tbsp neutral-flavoured oil (peanut oil)
150g pork mince
Sea salt, to taste
3 Spring onion
2 garlic cloves
1 heaped tbsp peanut butter
¼ cup (60ml) soy sauce
2 tbsp rice vinegar
1 lime, juice
2 tsp chilli crisp
1 packet, soft udon noodles
47826753bd1e091a50ecb431ec08d6358d4bae8f.instructions:
Place a medium pot half filled with lightly salted water onto the boil.
Finely slice the spring onions. Keep the white and green parts separate and set both aside.
Peel, crush and finely chop the garlic then set aside.
Heat a medium saucier over high heat. Add the oil and let it heat for 30 seconds. Add the pork mince, breaking it apart with a wooden spatula once it hits the pan. Spread it into a single layer and season with a pinch of salt.
Sear for 4-5 minutes until golden brown on all sides.
Add the sliced spring onion whites and garlic then stir through the pork.
Add the peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar and lime juice. Use the spatula to break up the peanut butter and emulsify it into the sauce. Add 2-3 tbsp of boiling water from the noodle pot and continue cooking for a further 2-3 minutes. At this stage you want the sauce to be slightly looser than you want the final dish, since the noodles will absorb some of the liquid.
Add in the chilli crisp, stir and turn the element off.
Add the packet of udon to the boiling water and cook until tender. Use tongs or chopsticks to stir the noodles while boiling to prevent clumping (for fresh noodles 1-3 minutes or dried 9-10 minutes).
Use tongs to carefully remove the udon noodles from the boiling water and transfer them into the sauce pan. Add the sliced spring onion greens and toss the noodles through the peanut butter sauce.
If the sauce feels too thick, add another splash of the noodle water. It should be glossy and just coat the noodles. Serve immediately.

4ffebff138e59c4350f931f2442a9ebd5fc68ddc.title: Cacio e Pepe
4ffebff138e59c4350f931f2442a9ebd5fc68ddc.text: Cacio e Pepe is pasta at its most stripped-back and brilliant – just spaghetti, pecorino, and black pepper. It’s quick, comforting, and a proper lesson in how simple ingredients, treated right, can be unbeatable. Perfect for a solo dinner when you want maximum payoff for minimal fuss.
4ffebff138e59c4350f931f2442a9ebd5fc68ddc.author: Andy
4ffebff138e59c4350f931f2442a9ebd5fc68ddc.ingredients:
120g spaghetti
1.5 tsp fresh ground black pepper
55g pecorino cheese, grated
salt
4ffebff138e59c4350f931f2442a9ebd5fc68ddc.instructions:
Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add spaghetti and swirl until fully submerged.
Cook pasta for 8 minutes, then pour off 250ml (1 cup) of pasta water into a heatproof jug. Continue cooking pasta for 2 more minutes, then strain.
Add an ice cube to the jug to bring the pasta water temperature down (ideally to 70°C).
Toast the pepper in a deep frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute, until aromatic. Turn off heat.
Place the cheese in a medium bowl and stir in the reserved pasta water 60ml (¼ cup) at a time, until the cheese has melted.
Pour cheese mixture into frying pan, making sure the pan is not too hot but not cold, and stir to combine with pepper, then add the pasta and begin stirring vigorously until mixture emulsifies and becomes a sauce, about 2-3 minutes.
Serve immediately.

14d938d8521e64497913c45f15e442c1e02e03f0.title: Māori Toroī
14d938d8521e64497913c45f15e442c1e02e03f0.text: Toroī is a traditional Māori side dish from Aotearoa (New Zealand), classically made with mussels or pipis and pūhā or watercress, then fermented until sour. This is my simplified home version where I skip the ferment and instead dress the mussels and watercress with garlic, chilli, salt and vinegar to get a similar bright, briny, slightly sour flavour served fresh from the fridge. Serve it on crackers, on toasted sourdough, alongside pan-seared white fish, over steamed rice, or at a hāngī. Ingredient NotesMussels: Try to find fresh, live mussels from a fishmonger or seafood counter. They should smell like the sea, not fishy, and any shells that are open should snap closed when tapped. Most farmed mussels come debearded, but check as you shell them and pull any stragglers off. Green-lipped mussels from New Zealand are the traditional choice if you can get them. Watercress: A peppery, mustard-family leafy green that grows in cold running waterways. In Australia it’s commercially available at specialty fruit and veg grocers. Store it in a bowl of cold water in the fridge, change the water daily, and it’ll keep for 3 to 4 days. If you can't find watercress or pūhā, you can substitute these for any bitter leafy green such as rocket, mustard greens, Dandelion Greens or even silverbeet. Bird’s eye chilli: I like to add some heat to this dish so keep the seeds in for extra spice or slice them out for a milder version. A red serrano, long red or dried chilli flakes all work as substitutes. Skip the chilli altogether if you’d rather it milder. EquipmentChopping boardChef’s knifeLarge pot with a lid (for the mussels)Second large pot (for blanching the watercress)ColanderTwo large bowls (one for the ice bath)Clean jar with a lid
14d938d8521e64497913c45f15e442c1e02e03f0.author: Andy
14d938d8521e64497913c45f15e442c1e02e03f0.ingredients:
1kg live mussels, cleaned and debearded
¼ cup (60ml) water (for steaming)
2 large bunches (approximately 300g) watercress
1 garlic clove, peeled and finely sliced
1 bird’s eye chilli, finely sliced
¼ tsp sea salt
1½ tbsp white distilled vinegar
14d938d8521e64497913c45f15e442c1e02e03f0.instructions:
Run the mussels under cold running water for 30 minutes to rinse out any grit or dirt.
Drain the mussels in a colander and discard the rinsing water. Place them in a large pot with the ¼ cup of water. Fit with a lid and place over medium heat.
Cook for 5 minutes, or until all the mussels have opened. Turn off the heat and strain through a colander, reserving the cooking liquid in a separate bowl.
Rest the mussels at room temperature for 10 minutes until cool enough to handle. Remove the meat from the shells. Discard any mussels that stayed shut. Pull off any beards you find as you go (most farmed mussels come debearded, but check).
Slice each mussel into 4 or 5 pieces, roughly 5mm thick. Place into a clean mixing bowl and transfer to the fridge while you prep the watercress.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Half-fill a large bowl with ice water.
Pick the watercress leaves off the tough stems. Thick stems are fibrous, the leaves and thin stems are what you want. Discard the woody stems.
Add the watercress to the boiling water and blanch for 30 seconds. Strain through a colander, then transfer straight into the ice water to stop the cooking. Stir to cool evenly.
Strain again and squeeze out as much water as you can with your hands.
Roughly chop the watercress on a board and add to the bowl with the mussels.
Add the sliced garlic, chilli, salt and vinegar to the bowl. Mix well.
Taste and adjust the seasoning to your liking.
Transfer to a clean jar. If the mussels and watercress aren’t fully submerged, top up with the reserved mussel cooking liquid. Seal with a lid.
Serve straight away or refrigerate. Best eaten cold from the fridge.

3acfbf76ea50a6aba8321749e4b5e97c838b4b4c.title: Chimichurri Sauce
3acfbf76ea50a6aba8321749e4b5e97c838b4b4c.text: I think chimichurri sauce is my favourite steak sauce. It comes from Argentina and is made with fresh herbs, garlic, oregano, vinegar and oil. It's perfect for drizzling over grilled meats, fish, veggies, or even on a piece of sourdough. It's very quick to make but it will need 2 hours to sit at room temp before serving. This allows the vinegar and salt to draw the flavours out of the herbs and bring everything together. Ingredient NotesFlat-leaf parsley: Also called Italian or continental parsley. You want to get bright green, fresh leaves and you need 1 bunch. We're only using the leaves in this recipe so you can save the stems for stock. Red wine vinegar: You want to use a good quality red wine vinegar as it plays a big part of the flavour. You can also use a Sherry vinegar. Fresh chilli: Cayenne, red serrano, long red or any medium-heat chilli will work. If you want it mild just use half a chilli, and if you want more heat add a whole chilli or a birds eye chilli. Extra virgin olive oil (EVOO): This is another key component so I would recommend using a good quality EVOO. EquipmentSharp Chef's knifeChopping boardMedium mixing bowl
3acfbf76ea50a6aba8321749e4b5e97c838b4b4c.author: Andy
3acfbf76ea50a6aba8321749e4b5e97c838b4b4c.ingredients:
1 small bunch flat-leaf parsley
½ red chilli
2 garlic cloves
½ tsp dried oregano
3 tbsp (1.5 fl oz) extra virgin olive oil
2 tbsp(1 fl oz) red wine vinegar
½ tsp salt, plus more to taste
3acfbf76ea50a6aba8321749e4b5e97c838b4b4c.instructions:
Pick the parsley leaves off the stem. Discard the stem and finely slice the leaves. Set aside.
Stack the leaves, roll them tightly and slice into fine ribbons (chiffonade). Set aside.
Remove the top of the chilli, slice in half lengthwise. Remove and discard the seeds. Finely dice and set aside. This recipe only requires half a red chilli, if you like it spicier, use a whole one.
Peel, crush and finely dice the garlic.
Combine the parsley, chilli, garlic, oregano, olive oil, red wine vinegar and salt in a medium bowl Mix well. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Leave the chimichurri to sit at room temperature for at least 2 hours (and up to 4) before serving.

0006be6451bf5616f8d0320a90c0ef8f2c33ddba.title: Tomato Relish
0006be6451bf5616f8d0320a90c0ef8f2c33ddba.text: In my opinion, homemade tomato relish beats anything from a jar. All you need is some ripe tomatoes, onion, garlic, chilli, apple cider vinegar, salt, brown sugar and soy sauce (for some depth). It's all cooked in one pot for about an hour and then you have a delicious relish you can use on eggs, sandwiches, burgers or a cheeseboard. Ingredient NotesTomatoes: We want ripe tomatoes for this recipe, and they can even be a little overripe if you have some sitting around in the fridge. I generally use Roma or Truss tomatoes but any variety will work. The reason you don't want unripe tomatoes is that they haven't developed their full flavours so the relish can end of being a little flat or bland. Dried chilli: This recipe includes one whole dried chilli to give the relish a bit of warmth. If you want to add more spice, slice the dried chilli open before tossing it into the pot. This allows the seeds to release and mix directly into the relish. If you want no spice, just leave the chilli out. Brown sugar: I use brown sugar for this recipe because it gives you that light caramel flavour that goes really well with the relish. That being said, any sugar will work to balance the acidity of the vinegar and tomato. Because we’re using such a small amount you don’t notice the sweetness like you can with some commercial brands of relish. The flavour should be sharp, umami and well balanced but not sweet. Soy Sauce: Soy sauce adds the depth of flavour and savoury umami that you won’t get just by adding salt alone. To make this recipe gluten free, swap the soy sauce for tamari to achieve a very similar result. EquipmentChopping board Chef's knife Medium pot Spatula or wooden spoonSterile jar with sealable lid
0006be6451bf5616f8d0320a90c0ef8f2c33ddba.author: Andy
0006be6451bf5616f8d0320a90c0ef8f2c33ddba.ingredients:
5 ripe tomatoes
4 cloves garlic
1 brown onion
1 dried chilli (more for increased heat)
1 tbsp brown sugar
1 tbsp apple cider vinegar
2 tbsp soy sauce
1/4 tsp sea salt
¼ cup water
0006be6451bf5616f8d0320a90c0ef8f2c33ddba.instructions:
Finely dice the tomatoes and set aside.
Peel, crush and finely dice the garlic. Peel and finely dice the onion.
Add the tomato, garlic, onion, dried chilli, brown sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, salt and water to a medium pot.
Place the pot over low-medium heat, lid off. Simmer gently for 35-40 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes to stop the base from catching. You’re looking for a consistency somewhere between a sauce and a jam.
Turn the heat off, then taste and adjust with more salt if needed.
Carefully spoon the warm relish into a sterile jar and seal with a lid. Transfer to the fridge.The relish is best enjoyed the following day one the flavours have had time to mature.

ec3872da37f2a4cb569aa60d53be63fb811364e6.title: Rocky Road
ec3872da37f2a4cb569aa60d53be63fb811364e6.text: Rocky road is one of those things that always disappears first at a Christmas gathering. My version leans into the classic Australian combination: macadamias, Turkish delight and raspberry lollies, all suspended in milk chocolate. That mix of crunchy, chewy, and fruity is what makes it work. I use milk chocolate as the base because it sets with the right texture, firm enough to slice cleanly without being brittle, and it balances the sweetness of the marshmallows and lollies without tipping into cloying. The technique is simple but the order matters. I pour half the melted chocolate into the tin first, then scatter all the mix-ins over it, then pour the remaining chocolate over the top. This gets everything suspended through the chocolate rather than sitting on a flat base. You get a much better distribution of mix-ins in every piece. Let it set completely in the fridge before you cut it, at least 2 to 4 hours, overnight if you can manage it. Cold chocolate slices cleanly. Warm chocolate drags and compresses, and you lose the layers. Ingredient NotesTurkish delight: You want Turkish delight without a chocolate coating for this. The boxed kind with a chocolate shell will add bitterness and throw the balance off. Look for plain rose or lemon Turkish delight from a quality grocer, deli, or Middle Eastern food store. Chop it into roughly 1.5cm pieces so you get a good amount of chew in each square without it dominating. It gets sticky on the knife, so a lightly oiled blade helps. Macadamias: Toasted macadamias give a rich, buttery crunch that pairs better with milk chocolate than almost any other nut. Buy them raw and toast in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, tossing regularly, until golden. Don’t skip the toasting. Raw macadamias are softer and lack that deep nutty flavour that makes them worth using. Let them cool completely before adding to the chocolate or they will cause it to seize. Milk chocolate: The chocolate is the base of this recipe so the quality shows. I use a good quality milk chocolate with at least 35% cocoa solids. Compound chocolate, the baking chocolate sold in blocks at the supermarket, sets harder and has a waxy texture compared to real chocolate. It will work in a pinch but the taste and mouthfeel are noticeably different. If you want to use dark chocolate instead, go for it, but the result will be more bitter and will set harder. A 50/50 mix of milk and dark is a good middle ground. EquipmentChopping boardChef’s knifeHeatproof bowlSaucepanWooden spoon or spatula20cm square tinBaking paper
ec3872da37f2a4cb569aa60d53be63fb811364e6.author: Andy
ec3872da37f2a4cb569aa60d53be63fb811364e6.ingredients:
540g milk chocolate
150g marshmallows
125g (1 cup) macadamias, toasted and chopped
120g raspberry lollies
120g Turkish delight, chopped
25g (½ cup) toasted coconut flakes
150g Christmas M&Ms (or regular)
ec3872da37f2a4cb569aa60d53be63fb811364e6.instructions:
Place the chocolate in a heatproof bowl over a saucepan of simmering water, ensuring the base of the bowl does not touch the water.
Stir until the chocolate is melted and smooth.
Line a 20cm (8in) square tin with baking paper. Pour half of the chocolate into the base of the pan and tilt the pan to spread chocolate evenly.
Place the marshmallows, macadamias, raspberry lollies, Turkish delight, coconut flakes and half the m&ms in in the tin and evenly distribute.
Gently pour over the remaining chocolate then sprinkle over the rest of the m&ms.
Refrigerate for 2-4 hours, until set solid. Cut into small squares and enjoy!

72412121e7711c86ba01e62c80e8f73c982c607b.title: Crab Tagliolini (Tagliolini al Granchio)
72412121e7711c86ba01e62c80e8f73c982c607b.text: Tagliolini al granchio is a classic Italian coastal pasta and one of those dishes where the quality of what you buy matters more than how you cook it. A garlic and chilli-infused olive oil, fresh crab, a splash of white wine, lemon zest and parsley tossed through delicate egg pasta. It’s the kind of dish that looks like it might be harder than it is, but only takes 15 minutes to make at home. Ingredient NotesFresh picked crab meat: The star of the dish. Look for fresh, hand-picked crab meat from a good fishmonger or seafood counter. A mix of white meat (for texture) and brown meat (for flavour) is ideal. Frozen picked crab thaws well and is a solid alternative. Avoid shelf-stable tinned crab, it’s usually too watery and mild for this dish. Fresh tagliolini: A very thin, flat egg pasta from Northern Italy, similar to tagliatelle but narrower. Look for it fresh at Italian delis or larger supermarkets. If you can’t find it, fresh linguine or fettuccine are the closest swaps. Dried pasta works but the texture won’t be the same delicate chew. Extra virgin olive oil: Use a good one. This dish is essentially oil-based, so the flavour of the olive oil comes through more than in a heavier pasta. A grassy, peppery EVOO is ideal, but any good-quality oil you’d happily eat straight will work. Dry white wine: Something you’d happily drink. A pinot grigio, sauvignon blanc, dry riesling or a Verdicchio all work. Don’t reach for cheap cooking wine, the flavour ends up in the finished sauce so it has to be decent. EquipmentLarge pot (for boiling the pasta)Medium sauté pan or saucepanChopping boardChef’s knifeFine grater or microplane (for the lemon zest)Tongs
72412121e7711c86ba01e62c80e8f73c982c607b.author: Andy
72412121e7711c86ba01e62c80e8f73c982c607b.ingredients:
3½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1 garlic clove, lightly crushed
pinch of dried chilli flakes
300g fresh picked crab meat
100ml dry white wine
220g fresh tagliolini
1 lemon, zested
½ cup flat-leaf parsley leaves, finely sliced
sea salt, to taste
72412121e7711c86ba01e62c80e8f73c982c607b.instructions:
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil.
Finely slice the parsley leaves and set aside. Zest the lemon and set aside.
Add 2 tablespoons of the olive oil and the crushed garlic clove to a medium sauté pan over low heat. Infuse gently for 2 minutes, watching that the garlic doesn’t brown.
Add the chilli flakes and continue to infuse for another 2 minutes. Remove and discard the garlic clove. Turn the heat up to high.
Drop the tagliolini into the boiling water and stir to stop it clumping. Cook until al dente, around 2 to 3 minutes.
While the pasta cooks, add the crab meat to the sauté pan with another tablespoon of olive oil. Stir gently for 1 to 2 minutes to warm through, with a light pinch of salt. Once the crab has turned opaque, pour in the white wine and let it bubble hard for 30 seconds to cook off the raw alcohol.
Use tongs to lift the cooked pasta directly into the sauté pan with the crab. A little of the pasta cooking water coming with it is a good thing.
Toss through until the pasta is coated. Pull the pan off the heat.
Add the lemon zest, sliced parsley and the remaining half tablespoon of olive oil. Toss through once more. Taste and adjust the salt if needed.
Divide between two bowls and serve immediately.

7bfb2255d4d2b50dd728fd0626ab38d174845bf7.title: Fresh Tomato Ricotta Pasta and Breaded Chickpeas
7bfb2255d4d2b50dd728fd0626ab38d174845bf7.text: Fresh tomato pasta sauce is quick to make and even better when you add in some ricotta. It comes out light pink, extra creamy, but still filled with some nice, fresh tomato flavor. This pasta is really half chickpeas/half pasta, but that's what makes it extra filling.
7bfb2255d4d2b50dd728fd0626ab38d174845bf7.author: Justine Doiron
7bfb2255d4d2b50dd728fd0626ab38d174845bf7.ingredients:
1 (15.5 oz) can chickpeas (drained and rinsed)
1/4 cup Castelvetrano olives (pitted)
1 teaspoon Calabrian chili paste (half if you’re sensitive to heat)
1/4 cup breadcrumbs
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
Diamond Crystal kosher salt
Freshly cracked black pepper
1 medium (8 oz) beefsteak tomato
2 garlic cloves
2 tablespoons tomato paste
8 ounces pasta of choice
1/2 cup whole milk ricotta
1/4 cup fresh basil leaves (optional for topping)
7bfb2255d4d2b50dd728fd0626ab38d174845bf7.instructions:
Rinse and dry the chickpeas very well with a paper towel. Add them to a sauté pan with a tight-fitting lid.
Roughly chop 1/4 cup of olives and add them to the pan along with 1 teaspoon of Calabrian chili paste, 1/4 cup of breadcrumbs, and 1/4 cup of olive oil. Mix to combine.
Cover to avoid any chickpea drama (they tend to pop when the skins hit the oil in a certain way) and place the pan over medium heat. Cook for 7-8 minutes, shaking every 2 minutes or so. When you notice the chickpeas have stopped popping and you see some steam come out of the lid, move the pan off the heat and uncover. If the chickpeas are nicely golden and the breadcrumbs cling to them, they're ready. If they still need a bit of time, toast them covered in 2 minute increments until they are ready.
Bring a medium pot of water to a boil and season with 1 tablespoon salt.
In another 12-inch sauté pan, halve the fresh tomato and grate it with a box grater, discarding the skins. Grate in two garlic cloves, and add 2 tablespoons of tomato paste.
Add 8 ounces of pasta to the boiling water and cook according to the package instructions until al dente.
While the pasta boils, put the tomato mixture over medium heat, keeping it at a low simmer for 4-6 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Scoop the pasta directly into the tomato sauce and add 1/2 cup of ricotta. Add 1/2 cup of pasta water and stir, you want it to be a little runny, so add more pasta water as you’d like.
To serve, spoon the pasta onto 4 plates and top with the chickpeas. Garnish with fresh basil.
7bfb2255d4d2b50dd728fd0626ab38d174845bf7.nutrition:
Calories: 569 kcal
Carbs: 69 g
Fat: 18 g
Serving size: 1 bowl

af4bb200438a0f6825ec677273ffbfce52a2976e.title: The perfect chips
af4bb200438a0f6825ec677273ffbfce52a2976e.text: This super-simple homemade chips recipe shows you how to fry chips at home with brilliant results. Great dunked into ketchup or mayo – naughty!
af4bb200438a0f6825ec677273ffbfce52a2976e.author: Jamie Oliver
af4bb200438a0f6825ec677273ffbfce52a2976e.instructions:
Three obvious things are important on your journey to perfection – your choice of potato, your choice of oil and your choice of salt. For me, the Maris Piper potato wins every time, and you want to use nice large ones.
On oil, sunflower and sunseed are very efficient, and many people swear by using groundnut oil. But, if you’re after flavour, cooking chips in beef tallow (rendered beef fat you can get from your butcher) gives you better flavour and colour – the choice is yours.
Finally, on salt, being an Essex boy, in my house it has to be Maldon sea salt.
So down to business: chop 800g of Maris Piper potatoes into finger-sized chips, leaving the skin on – don’t be too exact.
Chip shops have massive industrial fryers, which you can’t recreate at home, so you need to use a large sturdy pan on a medium to high heat (unless you own a deep-fat fryer, of course). Your oil should be 8cm deep, but never fill your pan more than half full. If you don’t have a thermometer, use a raw chip, and as it starts to float and fry the temperature should be about 140°C, which is perfect for blanching.
Use a large metal sieve to gently lower the chips into the pan for around 8 minutes, or until soft but not coloured, then remove to a tray to cool.
Turn the heat up under the oil and return one blanched chip to the oil as a guide again. Once it’s floating and golden the temperature should be about 180°C, which is perfect for frying and will give you chips with those all-important crispy outsides and fluffy middles.
At this stage you may want to cook your chips in 2-portion batches, so you don’t decrease the temperature of the oil too much or overcrowd the pan. Fry the chips until beautifully golden, then remove to a bowl lined with kitchen paper, shake around a bit, season with sea salt and serve right away.
af4bb200438a0f6825ec677273ffbfce52a2976e.nutrition:
Calories: 330 calories
Protein: 4 g
Carbs: 34.8 g
Fat: 20.3 g
Fiber: 2.6 g
Sugar: 1.2 g
Sodium: 0.5 g

81e2b978e65d82789a2814e41d1652e59ebec3d3.title: Flavoured butters
81e2b978e65d82789a2814e41d1652e59ebec3d3.text: Frozen flavoured butters are a fun thing to make and have available, ready to add an incredible flavour injection to anything you’re cooking. Try one of these for Christmas!
81e2b978e65d82789a2814e41d1652e59ebec3d3.author: Jamie Oliver
81e2b978e65d82789a2814e41d1652e59ebec3d3.ingredients:
# GREEN BUTTER
1 lemon
250g unsalted butter
1 bunch of fresh flat-leaf parsley (30g)
50g watercress
1 tablespoon jarred or fresh grated horseradish
# ORANGE, THYME & CUMIN BUTTER
2 teaspoons cumin seeds
1 bunch of fresh thyme (20g)
1 orange
2 cloves of garlic
250g unsalted butter
# MEDITERRANEAN BUTTER
2 cloves of garlic
250g unsalted butter
100g sun-dried tomatoes
6 olives (stone out)
1 heaped tablespoon harissa paste
# CURRY BUTTER
2 cloves of garlic
250g unsalted butter
2 tablespoons medium curry powder
2 tablespoons dried curry leaves
2 tablespoons black mustard seeds
# SAGE & ONION BUTTER
2 cloves of garlic
1 medium onion
1 bunch of fresh sage (30g)
250g unsalted butter
81e2b978e65d82789a2814e41d1652e59ebec3d3.instructions:
Blitz up your chosen flavour combo as below, spoon it on to a sheet of greaseproof paper, roll it up, shape it into a log and twist the ends like a Christmas cracker, then freeze for 1 hour.
Get it out of the freezer, unwrap it and slice it 1cm thick, then rewrap and keep frozen until needed. This means you’ll be able to easily click off what you need, as and when you want it.
You could also spoon a dollop of butter between two small squares of greaseproof paper and press down to flatten it into a disc before freezing. They’re great for popping inside a steamer when cooking veg – as the butter melts, it’ll rain down through the steamer and impart incredible flavour.
81e2b978e65d82789a2814e41d1652e59ebec3d3.nutrition:
Calories: 164 calories
Protein: 0.6 g
Carbs: 1.4 g
Fat: 17.5 g
Fiber: 0.3 g
Sugar: 0.7 g
Sodium: 0.3 g

806ba82be317d5622c614dd390b6d4a4cd45de9e.title: Movie night veggie nachos
806ba82be317d5622c614dd390b6d4a4cd45de9e.text: Get movie night ready with Buddy’s veggie nachos. With black beans, sweetcorn, tomatoes and avo, these are bound to become your new favourite snack.
806ba82be317d5622c614dd390b6d4a4cd45de9e.author: Buddy Oliver
806ba82be317d5622c614dd390b6d4a4cd45de9e.ingredients:
1 x 160g tin of sweetcorn
6 spring onions
1 long red pepper
3 ripe tomatoes
optional: 1 red chilli
optional: ½ a bunch of coriander (15g)
2 limes
olive oil
4 wholewheat tortillas
1 x 400g tin of black beans
1 ripe avocado
50g feta cheese
natural yoghurt or sour cream, to serve
optional: chilli sauce, to serve
806ba82be317d5622c614dd390b6d4a4cd45de9e.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 180°C, and place a large non-stick frying pan on a high heat to heat up.
Drain the sweetcorn and trim the spring onions. Put the whole pepper, tomatoes, spring onions and chilli (if using) into the dry pan for 10 minutes, or until soft and charred, turning occasionally. Transfer the pepper and chilli (if using) to a bowl, cover and leave for 5 minutes. Remove the tomatoes and spring onions to a board to cool.
Tip the sweetcorn into the pan and cook for 2 minutes, then place in a separate bowl. Once cool enough to handle, roughly chop the tomatoes and spring onions and add them to the charred sweetcorn.
Peel, deseed and roughly chop the pepper and chilli (if using), pick and chop a few coriander leaves (if using), then add it all to the bowl with the juice of ½ a lime, a splash of olive oil and a pinch of sea salt.
Pile up the tortillas and cut, through the stack, into eight triangles (so you end up with 32 in total), then arrange in a single layer over two baking trays. Bake for 15 minutes, or until golden, turning halfway.
Drain and rinse the beans, pat dry with kitchen paper, then tip into the frying pan over a medium heat and leave for 5 minutes, shaking occasionally – you want them to pop open. Peel and destone the avocado, slice into chunks, then squeeze over the juice of ½ a lime.
Arrange the tortilla chips on a serving plate, top with the popped beans, tomato and pepper salsa and the dressed avo. Crumble over the feta, pick over the leftover coriander leaves (if using) and dot over the yoghurt or sour cream and the chilli sauce (if using). Cut the remaining lime into wedges for squeezing over.
806ba82be317d5622c614dd390b6d4a4cd45de9e.nutrition:

f04fd23e10eae7c8f5650bf167248d2a23ba9e56.title: Caprese chicken burgers
f04fd23e10eae7c8f5650bf167248d2a23ba9e56.text: Skip the takeaway with this budget-friendly chicken burger recipe. A impressive, 40-minute meal using clever hacks for maximum flavour on a budget.
f04fd23e10eae7c8f5650bf167248d2a23ba9e56.author: Jamie Oliver
f04fd23e10eae7c8f5650bf167248d2a23ba9e56.ingredients:
2 large sweet potatoes
olive oil
2 chicken thighs, skin on, bone in
½ teaspoon smoked paprika
2 brioche or wholemeal buns
1 ripe tomato
½ a ball of mozzarella cheese
4 leaves of soft round lettuce (80g)
# PESTO
½ a bunch of fresh basil (15g)
20g blanched almonds
10g Italian hard cheese
f04fd23e10eae7c8f5650bf167248d2a23ba9e56.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 200ºC/400ºF/gas 6.
Scrub the sweet potatoes (there’s no need to peel them), then slice into 1cm-thick chips. Toss on a large baking tray with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and a pinch of sea salt and black pepper, spread out into a single layer and bake for 35 minutes or until golden and cooked through.
Pull the skin off the chicken thighs and place it in a non-stick frying pan on a medium-high heat.
Carefully run the tip of a sharp knife along the chicken thigh bones, then cut around the end of each bone to remove (don’t throw the bones away – see tip). Lightly score the meat to open it out slightly, then season with the paprika and a small pinch of salt and pepper.
Place the chicken thighs in the pan next to the skin, pop a large piece of greaseproof paper on top and weigh down with a heavy pan, pressing down to flatten them. Cook for 12 minutes, or until charred and cooked through, turning halfway and removing the skin once it’s brown and crispy. Halve and toast the buns in the residual heat.
For the pesto, pick the basil leaves into a pestle and mortar, reserving the stalks and a few nice baby leaves, and bash with a pinch of salt. Add the almonds and hard cheese, drizzle in 2 tablespoons of oil and bash to a smooth paste.
Slice the tomato into thin rounds. Finely slice the basil stalks and sprinkle over the tomato with a pinch of salt and a tiny drizzle of oil. Slice up the mozzarella.
Slice the chicken in half across the middle at an angle. Spread the pesto over the bases of the buns, then layer up the tomato, lettuce and chicken. Lay the mozzarella on top, slice and add the crispy chicken skin, then sprinkle over the reserved basil leaves and pop the lids on. Serve with the sweet potato chips and tuck in!

4a246f28321d5a79219650271fc2b894d67a07e0.title: Chakalaka
4a246f28321d5a79219650271fc2b894d67a07e0.text: Master classic South African Chakalaka! A vibrant, spiced vegetable relish made with peppers, carrots, baked beans, and curry spices.
4a246f28321d5a79219650271fc2b894d67a07e0.author: Nokx Majozi
4a246f28321d5a79219650271fc2b894d67a07e0.ingredients:
½ spring cabbage (Hispi), finely sliced
1 yellow pepper, deseeded and diced
1 red pepper, deseeded and diced
4 large carrots, peeled and grated
5 tomatoes, finely chopped
3 tbsp vegetable oil
1 onion, finely chopped
8cm ginger, peeled and grated
2 garlic cloves, minced
2 tbsp curry powder
1 x 400g tin of baked beans
Sea salt and black pepper
Chopped parsley, to serve (optional)
4a246f28321d5a79219650271fc2b894d67a07e0.instructions:
Start by preparing the cabbage, peppers, carrots and tomatoes and set to one side.
Put the oil in a large saucepan and set over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for about 6–8 minutes, stirring regularly until soft and translucent.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 2–3 minutes to soften, then add the curry powder and cook for a further minute until it smells fragrant.
Add the cabbage, peppers, carrots and tomatoes and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring regularly to ensure nothing sticks.
Add the baked beans, including their juice, cover with the lid and cook for a further 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper, to taste.
Serve it on toast, on baked potatoes or with chicken or fish. Scatter over some parsley if you’d like a hit of green, but it isn’t strictly necessary. You can keep any leftover chakalaka in the fridge for 5 days.

27c609b1267a61478c7f612b62499be3025f2fc6.title: Bobotie
27c609b1267a61478c7f612b62499be3025f2fc6.text: Bring the flavours of Cape Town home with this classic South African Bobotie. Perfectly spiced beef mince topped with a rich, golden egg custard.
27c609b1267a61478c7f612b62499be3025f2fc6.author: Nokx Majozi
27c609b1267a61478c7f612b62499be3025f2fc6.ingredients:
Butter, for greasing
2 tbsp vegetable oil
2 large onions, finely chopped
2 garlic cloves, finely chopped
3cm ginger, peeled and finely chopped
3 tbsp curry powder
1 tsp ground cumin
2 tsp ground turmeric
1kg beef mince
3 tbsp tomato paste
3 tbsp apricot chutney (or mango chutney)
1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
50g ground almonds
250ml whole milk
4 medium slices of white bread
2 large eggs, beaten
4 bay leaves
Sea salt and black pepper
1 quantity of Yellow Rice, to serve
27c609b1267a61478c7f612b62499be3025f2fc6.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 180°C/fan 160°C and grease a 24 x 30cm rectangular ovenproof dish, or similarly sized round dish, with butter.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. When hot, add the onion and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring regularly, until soft and translucent. Then add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, cumin and turmeric and stir for 2–4 minutes until the garlic softens and the spices release their flavour.
Add the beef mince and cook, stirring, for 8–10 minutes until browned, breaking up any large lumps. Add the tomato paste, chutney, Worcestershire sauce and ground almonds and mix well. Season with salt and pepper and remove from the heat.
Pour the milk into a large bowl and add the bread. Leave to soak for 5 minutes, then scoop out the bread, squeezing the excess milk back into the bowl (keep this to one side). On a plate, use a fork to mash the bread until smooth, then add it to the pan and mix well.
Transfer the mince mixture into the prepared dish and smooth out the top with the back of a spoon.
Mix the reserved milk with the beaten eggs and season with salt and pepper. Pour the mixture over the top of the meat. Place the bay leaves on top and bake for 40–50 minutes, until the egg is set and the top is golden brown. Cut into portions and serve with Yellow Rice and a side salad.

a3c378330f883919e4eb040272841e802abe6c62.title: Chicken wings with mango
a3c378330f883919e4eb040272841e802abe6c62.text: Sweet, sticky and warm with spice, these wings are the ultimate crowd-pleaser. Coated in a vibrant mango glaze and cooked to perfection!
a3c378330f883919e4eb040272841e802abe6c62.author: Nokx Majozi
a3c378330f883919e4eb040272841e802abe6c62.ingredients:
500g chicken wings
# MARINADE
1 ripe mango, peeled, destoned and roughly chopped
2 garlic cloves, peeled
2 tsp paprika
2 limes, zest and juice
5 tbsp apple cider vinegar
4 tbsp honey
4 tbsp olive oil
2 tbsp chilli flakes
Sea salt and black pepper
# MANGO SALSA
1 ripe mango, peeled, destoned and cubed
1 small red onion, finely chopped
1 tomato, deseeded and finely chopped
A few sprigs coriander, leaves picked and, finely chopped
1 small red chilli, finely chopped
½ lemon, juice only
a3c378330f883919e4eb040272841e802abe6c62.instructions:
Start by making the marinade. In a food processor, put the mango, garlic, paprika, lime juice and apple cider vinegar. Blend together until smooth.
Transfer to a small saucepan over a medium heat and cook for about 10 minutes. Add the honey, oil, chilli flakes and lime zest and stir for another minute until it all comes together. Season to taste then remove from the heat and leave to cool on the side.
Pat the chicken wings dry using a piece of kitchen paper and transfer to a container that will fit in the fridge. Reserve a small bowlful of the marinade and add the rest to the wings, coating them well, then cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or ideally overnight. Set aside the reserved marinade to baste the chicken.
Light the braai 30 minutes before you want to cook. When you’re ready to cook and the coals are hot, lightly brush the grill with oil. If you can adjust the height of your grill, raise it to a medium height, otherwise move your coals to one side and place your chicken away from the coals so it cooks slowly.
Place the wings on the grill and cook for at least 30 minutes, turning them occasionally. Baste with the reserved marinade and cook for another 5 minutes, then check they are cooked by cutting to the bone. If the juices run clear, they are done; if it is still a bit pink, cook for a little longer. Transfer to a serving plate.

515bf03e926d2c2d1f10fc34642ba35dd0062706.title: Zombie
515bf03e926d2c2d1f10fc34642ba35dd0062706.text: The Zombie is a delicious rum cocktail mixed with tropical fruit flavours; Follow our simple zombie cocktail recipe for delicious results.
515bf03e926d2c2d1f10fc34642ba35dd0062706.author: Jamie Oliver
515bf03e926d2c2d1f10fc34642ba35dd0062706.ingredients:
2 parts Bacardi Carta Blanco
1⅓ parts Bacardi Oro
1 part Triple Sec Liqueur
2 parts sweet and sour mix (see tip)
2 parts orange juice
1 part grenadine (or Blue Curacao)
cubed ice
optional garnish: orange or lime slices, fresh mint cherries
515bf03e926d2c2d1f10fc34642ba35dd0062706.instructions:
Put lots of ice and all of the ingredients except the grenadine (or blue Curaçao) into a shaker.
Shake for about 20 seconds to chill the liquid really well, then strain the mix into the glass over ice (you could fill your glass with ice and pour the mix straight in, or - to look flash - strain it over ice separately and then add to a glass containing fresh ice).
Pour a little of the grenadine (or Blue Curaçao) over the drink so it floats on top – gently does it!
Serve with a garnish or two, if you like.

f0a350a3f5c5e49e2ac25dcb1e4205d54cbd0af2.title: Braised veal
f0a350a3f5c5e49e2ac25dcb1e4205d54cbd0af2.text: Looking for a gorgeous veal recipe? We've got you covered. With mushrooms, wine, leeks and cream this deliciously rich slow-cook dish can't fail to impress your guests.
f0a350a3f5c5e49e2ac25dcb1e4205d54cbd0af2.author: Andy Harris & Georgie Socratous
f0a350a3f5c5e49e2ac25dcb1e4205d54cbd0af2.ingredients:
1 large knob of butter
olive oil
1 x 2kg fillet of higher-welfare veal leg, tied with string
2 onions
2 cloves of garlic
400g leeks
300g baby carrots
2 fresh bay leaves
350ml white wine
2 handfuls of mixed mushrooms
300ml double cream
f0a350a3f5c5e49e2ac25dcb1e4205d54cbd0af2.instructions:
Place a casserole pan on a medium heat and melt half the butter with a splash of oil. Season and brown the veal on all sides, then remove from pan and set aside.
Peel and finely slice the onions and garlic, then trim and cut the leeks into large chunks. Sauté in the same pan until soft but not coloured, then add the carrots and cook for a few minutes.
Make a space in the middle, and place in your veal, surrounded by the veg. Tuck the bay into the veal and pour in the wine and 100ml water.
Bring to the boil, then cover with a circle of greaseproof paper and simmer for 2 to 2 hours 30 minutes, till the veal is tender. Check the liquid level every 20 minutes or so, adding water as necessary.
When the veal is ready, place a frying pan on a medium-high heat with the remaining butter. Tear in the mushrooms and fry until they start to turn golden.
Season, and stir into the veal with the double cream. Bring back to the boil then simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, till reduced.
Transfer the veal to a board and slice. Serve with braised veg, buttered spätzli or noodles and cabbage gratin.

1517ea55ea4067003f9ed083e304f23300391882.title: Beef short ribs
1517ea55ea4067003f9ed083e304f23300391882.text: These incredibly tasty beef short ribs are well worth the wait.
1517ea55ea4067003f9ed083e304f23300391882.author: Jamie Oliver
1517ea55ea4067003f9ed083e304f23300391882.ingredients:
6 beef short ribs, bone in (approx 1.6kg)
2 heads of celery
6 carrots (600g total)
50g shelled unsalted walnut halves
½ x 345g jar of onion marmalade
500ml smooth ale
6 baking potatoes (1.5kg total)
creamed horseradish, to serve
1517ea55ea4067003f9ed083e304f23300391882.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 160°C/325°F/gas 3.
Put a large shallow casserole pan on a medium-high heat and brown the ribs all over, turning with tongs, for about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim the celery and use a speed-peeler to remove the stringy outsides. Chop off the bottom 12cm of each and cut lengthways into quarters, then finely slice the remaining stalks, reserving any nice leaves. Peel the carrots, leaving them whole.
Once the ribs are browned, remove them to a bowl for a moment. Put all the celery and the carrots into the pan with the walnuts and onion marmalade and toss to coat. Season with sea salt and black pepper.
Pour in 600ml of water and the ale, then nestle the ribs back into the pan, making sure they’re submerged. Cover with a sheet of damp greaseproof paper and roast for 4 hours, or until the meat pulls easily away from the bone, basting halfway.
Scrub the potatoes, prick all over with a fork and bake alongside the ribs for the last 1 hour 30 minutes.
Skim any fat off the ribs, remove the bones and any wobbly bits and serve with dollops of horseradish, sprinkled with any reserved celery leaves, and the jacket spuds on the side.

7e76040306ede8b5da136c803966e7f9c9def59b.title: Dukkah roast chicken & smashed aubergine
7e76040306ede8b5da136c803966e7f9c9def59b.text: A family-style roast chicken that uses seasonal veg like aubergines and squash and North African flavours to give you a proper autumnal alternative to the classic Sunday roast.
7e76040306ede8b5da136c803966e7f9c9def59b.author: Jamie Oliver
7e76040306ede8b5da136c803966e7f9c9def59b.ingredients:
# CHICKEN
2 pomegranates
olive oil
3 preserved lemons
1-2 fresh red chillies
1 bunch of fresh rosemary (20g)
1 x 1.6kg free-range whole chicken
extra virgin olive oil
1 tablespoon runny honey
3 tablespoons dukkah
# SMASHED AUBERGINE
1kg aubergines
1 bulb of garlic
2 tablespoons tahini
1 lemon
½ a bunch of fresh flat-leaf parsley (15g)
# ROAST SQUASH
1-1.5kg mixture of squash, such as acorn, kabocha, butternut
½ a bunch of fresh sage (10g)
# COUSCOUS
300g couscous
1 sprig of fresh oregano
7e76040306ede8b5da136c803966e7f9c9def59b.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 180°C/350°F/gas 4.
Get a roasting tray that will fit the chicken fairly snugly. Halve 1 pomegranate, squeeze all the juice through your fingers into the tray and drizzle in 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Halve, deseed and finely chop the preserved lemons and place in the tray. Roughly chop and add the chilli, strip in the rosemary leaves, and season with sea salt and black pepper.
Add the chicken to the tray and rub that lovely flavour over the bird, getting into all the nooks and crannies. Set aside.
Prick the aubergines, place in a roasting tray with the unpeeled bulb of garlic.
Scrub the squash (there’s no need to peel it), then carefully cut in half and use a spoon to scrape out the seeds. Cut into chunky moon-shaped wedges, then add to a large roasting tray. Season with salt and plenty of pepper, pick in the sage leaves, drizzle with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and toss together well. Arrange them so they’re flesh-side up, like little boats.
Pour 150ml of water into the tray around the chicken and place in the oven, along with the aubergine and squash.
Roast for 1 hour 20 minutes, or until the aubergines are blackened, blistered and soft, the squash is tender, and the chicken is golden and cooked through. Baste the chicken with the tray juices halfway through.
When the chicken is nearly ready, prepare the couscous. Place in a bowl with the oregano, a pinch of salt and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil. Pour in just enough boiling kettle water to cover, pop a plate on top and leave to fluff up.
Once ready, remove the chicken and veg from the oven, leaving the chicken to rest in its tray for 30 minutes.
Halve the aubergines lengthways, scoop out the middles into a large bowl, discarding the skin, then squash and break up the flesh. Squeeze the soft garlic flesh out of their skins into the bowl.
Add the tahini and squeeze in the lemon juice. Finely chop and add the parsley, stalks and all, drizzle with 1 tablespoon of extra virgin olive oil, then season to perfection, tasting and tweaking, and mix well.
Place the couscous onto a serving platter and spoon over the smashed aubergine. Place the chicken on top, drizzle with the honey and scatter over the dukkah, then arrange the squash around the sides. Halve the remaining pomegranate then, holding one half so it’s cut-side down in your fingers, bash with the back of a spoon so all the seeds tumble over the chicken (save the remaining pomegranate half for another day). Serve it all up with fragrant chicken juices from the tray – heaven!

39b739990ef891ed3c5013fbcc1c6ce6a64b5b90.title: Prosecco, pear & blackberry punch
39b739990ef891ed3c5013fbcc1c6ce6a64b5b90.text: This beautiful punch recipe is a nostalgic favourite with a twist! Blackberries, cinnamon, orange zest, prosecco and warming spices - so festive!
39b739990ef891ed3c5013fbcc1c6ce6a64b5b90.author: Jamie Oliver
39b739990ef891ed3c5013fbcc1c6ce6a64b5b90.ingredients:
300g blackberries, fresh or frozen
5 cloves
1 stick of cinnamon
2 pieces of orange zest
1 star anise
2 pears
300ml pear-flavoured vodka
750ml prosecco (Martini prosecco if possible)
39b739990ef891ed3c5013fbcc1c6ce6a64b5b90.instructions:
Add a handful of the blackberries to a heatproof bowl and squish them to release their juices, then add the rest, along with the spices, orange zest and 300ml boiling water. Core and slice the pears, then add them to the water. Give it a good stir, then leave to steep for at least 8 hours, or overnight.
Pour the infusion into the Showstopper bowl, then half-fill it with ice. Go in with the vodka and prosecco, give it a gentle stir, then serve it straight away.

29badd340a1169e6e4143e2d8bb912335ea15ebe.title: Spider pizzas
29badd340a1169e6e4143e2d8bb912335ea15ebe.text: With melty cheese, passata and olives, these mini spider pizzas are scarily good. Plus, they couldn't be easier to make with the kids.
29badd340a1169e6e4143e2d8bb912335ea15ebe.author: Jamie Oliver
29badd340a1169e6e4143e2d8bb912335ea15ebe.ingredients:
3 wholemeal tortilla wraps
6 tablespoons passata
50g Cheddar cheese
18 black pitted olives
29badd340a1169e6e4143e2d8bb912335ea15ebe.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 180°C/350°F/gas 4.
Use a cookie cutter to cut 12 small rounds from the wholemeal tortillas and lay them on a baking tray.
Spread the passata over each round and grate over the Cheddar.
To make the spiders’ bodies, cut 12 of the olives in half lengthways and place two halves on top of the pizzas side-by-side.
To make the spiders’ legs, cut the remaining olives in half lengthways then finely slice and arrange four slices on each side so they look like legs.
Bake for 2 to 3 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling.

0ef440ed115e7064eca3a21a06054e12c2ec072c.title: Easy Mayonnaise
0ef440ed115e7064eca3a21a06054e12c2ec072c.author: Joshua Weissman
0ef440ed115e7064eca3a21a06054e12c2ec072c.ingredients:
2 large egg yolks
1.5 Tbsp (23g) Dijon mustard
1 Tbsp (15mL) lemon juice
2 Tbsp (30mL) water
Kosher salt, to taste
1 cup (240mL) neutral oil (canola, avocado, vegetable)
0ef440ed115e7064eca3a21a06054e12c2ec072c.instructions:
Add the egg yolks, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, water, and salt to a tall, narrow quart container. Pour the neutral oil over top and allow it to settle for a few seconds.
Place an immersion blender at the very bottom of the container. Blend without moving the blender until the mixture at the bottom becomes thick, creamy, and emulsified, about 10-15 seconds.
With the blender still running, slowly lift it toward the surface to incorporate the remaining oil. Continue blending until completely smooth and emulsified. Season to taste with additional salt, if needed.

16daa9f4b152f42ca6f5336019b745119afed97f.title: Taco Bell Fire Sauce
16daa9f4b152f42ca6f5336019b745119afed97f.author: Joshua Weissman
16daa9f4b152f42ca6f5336019b745119afed97f.ingredients:
1 ancho chili, stemmed and deseeded
3 guajillo chilies, stemmed and deseeded
2.5 cups (600mL) boiling water
½ tsp (1g) onion powder
1 tsp (3g) cayenne powder
1 tsp (3g) smoked paprika
1.5 tsp (5g) ground cumin
4 cloves garlic, peeled
2 Tbsp (30mL) white distilled vinegar
Kosher salt, to taste
6 oz (170g) tomato paste
16daa9f4b152f42ca6f5336019b745119afed97f.instructions:
Add the ancho and guajillo chilies to a small mixing bowl, then pour over the boiling water. Let sit until rehydrated and softened, about 10 minutes. The chilies should tear easily by hand. Do not discard the soaking liquid.
Transfer the softened chilies to the base of a blender along with the onion powder, cayenne, paprika, cumin, garlic, vinegar, salt to taste, and tomato paste. Blend on medium speed, gradually increasing to high, until as smooth as possible. With the blender running, gradually stream in the reserved chili soaking liquid until completely incorporated and smooth. Season again to taste with salt.
Optionally, for a smoother, more Taco Bell-like consistency, pass the sauce through a fine-mesh strainer. Let cool completely before refrigerating.

9febf6fdd4291049f4d7423ee7e01b75bc09ef86.title: Raising Cane’s Cane's Sauce
9febf6fdd4291049f4d7423ee7e01b75bc09ef86.author: Joshua Weissman
9febf6fdd4291049f4d7423ee7e01b75bc09ef86.ingredients:
¾ cup (180g) mayonnaise (recipe)
5 Tbsp (75g) ketchup
1.5 Tbsp (23mL) Worcestershire sauce
2 tsp (10mL) shirodashi
½ tsp (1g) freshly cracked black pepper
Kosher salt, to taste
2-3 cloves garlic, finely grated
9febf6fdd4291049f4d7423ee7e01b75bc09ef86.instructions: In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, ketchup, Worcestershire, shirodashi, black pepper, salt to taste, and garlic until evenly combined. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to develop. Stir well before serving.

c711ee77dd0cc42ac05637dc86cda258baec4db8.title: Wendy’s Honey BBQ Sauce
c711ee77dd0cc42ac05637dc86cda258baec4db8.author: Joshua Weissman
c711ee77dd0cc42ac05637dc86cda258baec4db8.ingredients:
¾ cup (180g) ketchup
¼ cup (60g) honey
2 Tbsp (40g) molasses
¼ tsp (<1g) onion powder
½ tsp (1g) garlic powder
2 tsp (7g) smoked paprika
2½ tsp (8g) freshly cracked black peppercorns
2 Tbsp (30mL) distilled white vinegar
1 Tbsp (15mL) Worcestershire sauce
2 Tbsp (30g) Dijon mustard
1 tsp (5mL) liquid smoke
Kosher salt, to taste
Water, as needed for consistency
c711ee77dd0cc42ac05637dc86cda258baec4db8.instructions:
Combine the ketchup, honey, molasses, onion powder, garlic powder, paprika, black pepper, vinegar, Worcestershire, Dijon, and liquid smoke in a small saucepan.
Add a small splash of water to thin to your desired consistency. Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, then reduce to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3-4 minutes. Season to taste with salt.
Let cool completely before serving. For the best flavor, cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.

331cdfc313b6890325ead1de8d9345145069dd88.title: Popeyes Blackened Ranch Sauce
331cdfc313b6890325ead1de8d9345145069dd88.author: Joshua Weissman
331cdfc313b6890325ead1de8d9345145069dd88.ingredients:
1 cup (240g) mayonnaise
½ cup (120g) crème fraîche, or sour cream
1 Tbsp (15g) Dijon mustard
½ cup (120mL) buttermilk
2 Tbsp (6g) fresh chives, very thinly sliced
¼ cup (10g) fresh parsley, finely chopped
2 Tbsp (6g) fresh dill, finely chopped
1 tsp (3g) smoked paprika
½ tsp (1g) onion powder
¾ tsp (2g) cayenne pepper
¼ tsp (<1g) celery powder
3 cloves garlic, grated
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
¼-½ tsp (~1g) MSG
331cdfc313b6890325ead1de8d9345145069dd88.instructions:
In a large mixing bowl, combine the mayonnaise, crème fraîche, Dijon, buttermilk, chives, parsley, dill, paprika, onion powder, cayenne, celery powder, grated garlic, salt and pepper to taste, and MSG. Whisk until thoroughly combined and smooth.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving to allow the herbs and spices to bloom. For the best flavor, refrigerate overnight.

636ccafa6ee86ba0654e145dc186f763212dc7c1.title: KFC Sauce
636ccafa6ee86ba0654e145dc186f763212dc7c1.author: Joshua Weissman
636ccafa6ee86ba0654e145dc186f763212dc7c1.ingredients:
½ cup (120g) mayonnaise
2 Tbsp (30g) ketchup
2 Tbsp (30g) honey
2 Tbsp (30g) yellow mustard
2 Tbsp (30g) Dijon mustard
2 tsp (10mL) Worcestershire sauce
½ tsp (1g) paprika
Pinch of cayenne pepper, *optional
½ tsp (1g) garlic powder
¼ tsp (<1g) onion powder
2 tsp (10mL) white distilled vinegar
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
636ccafa6ee86ba0654e145dc186f763212dc7c1.instructions:
Add the mayonnaise, ketchup, honey, yellow mustard, Dijon, Worcestershire, paprika, cayenne (if using), garlic powder, onion powder, vinegar, and salt and black pepper to taste to a medium mixing bowl. Whisk until completely smooth and evenly combined.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving for the best flavor.

8c79b2230b21275ab16e3a65d92dbbb87221b714.title: McDonald’s Sweet and Sour Sauce
8c79b2230b21275ab16e3a65d92dbbb87221b714.author: Joshua Weissman
8c79b2230b21275ab16e3a65d92dbbb87221b714.ingredients:
¼ cup (60g) apricot jam
¼ cup (60g) peach jam
1 Tbsp (13g) light brown sugar
1 tsp (5mL) fresh lemon juice
2 Tbsp (30mL) sherry vinegar
1 Tbsp (15mL) shirodashi
2 tsp (10g) yellow mustard
2 tsp (5g) cornstarch
2 Tbsp (30mL) water
Kosher salt, to taste
8c79b2230b21275ab16e3a65d92dbbb87221b714.instructions:
Add the apricot jam, peach jam, brown sugar, lemon juice, sherry vinegar, shirodashi, yellow mustard, and salt to taste to a small saucepan. Place over medium heat and bring to a simmer, stirring often.
Meanwhile, whisk together the cornstarch and water in a small bowl until completely smooth. Once the sauce reaches a simmer, whisk in the cornstarch slurry and cook, whisking constantly, until thickened and glossy, about 20-30 seconds.
Remove from the heat and let cool completely before serving. The sauce will continue to thicken as it cools.

d18f8f38b894e937fd5383ff9fa48a85a99deb42.title: Whataburger Spicy Ketchup
d18f8f38b894e937fd5383ff9fa48a85a99deb42.author: Joshua Weissman
d18f8f38b894e937fd5383ff9fa48a85a99deb42.ingredients:
2 red jalapenos
1 cup (240g) ketchup
1 Tbsp (15mL) apple cider vinegar
1 tsp (5mL) Worcestershire sauce
1 tsp (3g) smoked paprika
½ tsp (1g) garlic powder
¼ tsp (<1g) onion powder
1 tsp (3g) cayenne pepper
2 tsp (10g) honey
Kosher salt, to taste
d18f8f38b894e937fd5383ff9fa48a85a99deb42.instructions:
Char the jalapenos on all sides over an open flame or under a broiler, then transfer to a bowl and cover with plastic wrap. Let steam until softened, about 5 minutes. Wipe away the charred skin with a damp paper towel. Remove and discard the stems, then transfer the jalapenos to the base of a blender.
Add the ketchup, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, honey, and salt to taste.
Blend on high speed until completely smooth, scraping down the sides of the blender as needed. Taste and adjust the seasoning with additional salt, vinegar, or cayenne as desired.
For the best flavor, cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.

3f16b2ccb3eb38bb1091447303ade6edf8bdb53b.title: Best Ever Chewy Brownies
3f16b2ccb3eb38bb1091447303ade6edf8bdb53b.author: Joshua Weissman
3f16b2ccb3eb38bb1091447303ade6edf8bdb53b.ingredients:
6½ Tbsp (92g) unsalted butter
½ cup (150g) dulce de leche
8 oz (227g) 70% dark chocolate, finely chopped
1 large egg
1 large egg yolk
2 tsp (10mL) pure vanilla extract
2½ Tbsp (38mL) vegetable oil
⅛ tsp (<1g) baking soda
½ tsp (2g) fine sea salt
1¼ cups (150g) powdered sugar
¼ cup (25g) unsweetened cocoa powder
5 Tbsp (40g) all-purpose flour
4 oz (113g) 70% dark chocolate, roughly chopped
3f16b2ccb3eb38bb1091447303ade6edf8bdb53b.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 325°F (163°C). Add the butter to a small saucepan over medium heat and cook, swirling occasionally, until the milk solids turn golden brown and the butter smells nutty and aromatic. Remove from the heat.
While the butter is still hot, whisk in the dulce de leche. It may resist incorporating at first, but continue whisking until mostly smooth. Add the 8 oz (227g) of finely chopped chocolate and whisk until completely melted, smooth, and glossy. Set aside to cool slightly.
In a separate large bowl, whisk together the egg, egg yolk, vanilla extract, vegetable oil, baking soda, and salt until smooth and homogeneous. Slowly whisk in the warm chocolate mixture until fully incorporated.
