400g tin chopped tomatoes
2 tbsp neutral flavoured oil
1 cinnamon stick
7 green cardamom pods
1 tsp ground cumin
2 tsp garam masala
0.5-2 teaspoons Kashmiri chilli powder
2 tbsp greek yoghurt, to serve
coriander to garnish
41de4bff4035b72d69c2bab987621d9c522ef304.instructions:
Start by placing the rice on to cook.
Next, in a large heavy-based pot over high heat, add the oil, cinnamon stick and cardamom pods, and cook this for 3-4 minutes or until fragrant.
Add the onions and a pinch of salt, and cook them down for 4-5 minutes moving them constantly.
Once the onions have good colour on them, add the chicken and stir through.
Add a little more salt and the rest of the dry spices (cumin, masala, chilli powder), the ginger and garlic, and stir through and let toast for a minute. Now, add ½ cup of water and stir, getting any fond off the bottom of the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add the tin of tomatoes and then add some water to the tin and add to the pot to make sure you have all of it. Stir through and turn the heat to low and simmer for 4-5 minutes.
Add the sliced asparagus, stir through and simmer for another 2 minutes.
Serve over rice, with a dollop of yoghurt and garnish with coriander

fea042594de19e88dba8e9199ee6f7c55c69d40d.title: Glazed Tofu Rice Bowls with Sesame Cucumbers
fea042594de19e88dba8e9199ee6f7c55c69d40d.text: This is probably the easiest glazed tofu I have in my repertoire, you don't need to do much other than sear it and mix together a few condiments. Kecap manis is an Indonesian sweet soy sauce that can be hard to find, but even if you go through the trouble of ordering it online (Amazon and other big sellers stock it!), you'll be hooked on how much it can bring to a meal.
fea042594de19e88dba8e9199ee6f7c55c69d40d.author: Justine Doiron
fea042594de19e88dba8e9199ee6f7c55c69d40d.ingredients:
1 cup short grain white rice
1 16-ounce pack of extra-firm tofu
1/2 teaspoon gochugaru (optional)
Diamond Crystal kosher salt
Extra-virgin olive oil
2 medium Chinese eggplant
2 medium seedless cucumbers
1/2 teaspoon granulated sugar
1 teaspoon sesame oil
1 tablespoon white sesame seeds
1/3 cup kecap manis (or another variety of sweet soy sauce )
2 tablespoons sriracha
2 sprigs Thai basil (optional)
3-4 sprigs mint (optional, for serving )
fea042594de19e88dba8e9199ee6f7c55c69d40d.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425°F, then begin cooking 1 cup of rice in a rice cooker according to package instructions.
Drain a 16-ounce block of tofu, press out any excess moisture and cut it into 1-inch thick rectangular pieces. Put these in a bowl and toss with 1/2 teaspoon gochugaru and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Set aside.
Slice the tops off 2 medium Chinese eggplant, then slice them crosswise, alternating the angle of your knife so you have diagonal slices that give you 1-inch chunks. Add these to a quarter sheet pan, drizzle with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and season with 1/4 teaspoon salt. Roast these for 18-22 minutes, or until golden on the bottoms.
Thinly slice 2 cucumbers and add them to a bowl. Season with 1/2 teaspoon salt, mix, and set aside so they can release moisture.
While the cucumbers are sitting, sear the tofu. Put a large pan over medium heat and add enough olive oil to coat the surface (around 3 tablespoons). Sear the tofu for 3-4 minutes per side, or until deeply golden and crisp. Line a bowl with paper towels and transfer the pieces back in to drain.
Drain the cucumbers, squeezing them lightly to get out all the water. Season with 1/2 teaspoon sugar, 1 teaspoon sesame oil and 1 tablespoon white sesame seeds. Mix, taste and season as preferred.
Pull the paper towels out of the tofu bowl. Add in 1/3 cup kecap manis, 2 tablespoons sriracha, and tear in 2 sprigs of Thai basil leaves. Mix until the tofu is nicely sticky.
By now the eggplant should be roasted and the rice should be finished. To serve, pile the rice in a bowl, add a bit of the eggplant, a scoop of the cucumbers, and a scoop of the tofu. Serve with fresh mint on top.

c8d2f05065f37779b46181b7cd3ab0d339ccb46c.title: Peach Shortcakes with Lemon Vanilla Sugar
c8d2f05065f37779b46181b7cd3ab0d339ccb46c.text: Take my classic (easy!) shortcake dough and layer some peaches on top, and you have a shortcake that somehow mimics a danish, but is buttery, flaky and much simpler and quicker to make. Perfect for the end of stone fruit season (and I miss it already!).
c8d2f05065f37779b46181b7cd3ab0d339ccb46c.author: Justine Doiron
c8d2f05065f37779b46181b7cd3ab0d339ccb46c.ingredients:
# For the shortcakes
1 1/2 cups (210g) all-purpose flour
2 tablespoons (25g) granulated sugar
2 teaspoons baking powder
1/2 teaspoon Diamond Crystal kosher salt
1/3 cup (85g) salted butter (cold)
1/2 cup (120g) buttermilk
# For the peaches
1 large (9 oz) yellow peach
1 tablespoon cornstarch
1 tablespoon lemon juice
1 tablespoon brown sugar
# For the vanilla lemon sugar
1/2 teaspoon lemon zest
1/4 teaspoon vanilla extract
2 tablespoons turbinado sugar
c8d2f05065f37779b46181b7cd3ab0d339ccb46c.instructions:
In a large bowl whisk together 210 grams of flour, 25 grams of sugar, 2 teaspoons of baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon of salt.
Use a box grater to grate in 85 grams of salted butter. Toss to coat in the flour, pressing it in with my fingers.
Pour in 120 grams of buttermilk and mix into a shaggy dough.
Transfer the dough to a work surface and pat it down into a large circle, about 1/2 inch thick. Dust with flour as needed. Use a 3-inch round cutter to cut 5 circles. Transfer these to a parchment-lined sheet pan and place them in the fridge while you prep the rest of the recipe.
Preheat the oven to 375°F convection, or 400°F standard.
Thinly slice the peach and add it to a large bowl. Toss with 1 tablespoon of cornstarch, 1 tablespoon of lemon juice, and 1 tablespoon of brown sugar.
In a small dish, add 1/2 teaspoon of lemon zest, 1/4 teaspoon of vanilla extract, and 2 tablespoons of turbinado sugar. Scrunch together with your fingers until it’s the texture of wet sand.
Pull the shortcakes out of the fridge and use a spoon to make a big indent in the center of each. Layer 4-5 peach slices in the center. Sprinkle the vanilla lemon sugar all over the edges of the shortcakes and the peaches.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the edges of the shortcakes are very golden.
Serve warm.
c8d2f05065f37779b46181b7cd3ab0d339ccb46c.nutrition:
Calories: 329 kcal
Protein: 5 g
Carbs: 47 g
Fat: 13 g
Serving size: 1 shortcake

d54aedb9dfe06aece803d9ba4b5ef816c1f8d87f.title: Zucchini Burgers
d54aedb9dfe06aece803d9ba4b5ef816c1f8d87f.text: I think this may be my best veggie burger yet. Simple to mix and easy to cook, these burgers have enough protein to stay satisfying, and just a few vegetables - because we <3 vegetables. With the right bun and toppings (don't skip the slaw!), this tastes like a classic burger, and I think that's why I love it so much.
d54aedb9dfe06aece803d9ba4b5ef816c1f8d87f.author: Justine Doiron
d54aedb9dfe06aece803d9ba4b5ef816c1f8d87f.ingredients:
1 (9 oz) zucchini
1 (14 oz) pack firm tofu
1 teaspoon salt
2 scallions (sliced)
3 garlic cloves (grated)
2 tablespoons tomato paste
1/4 cup soy sauce
2 tablespoons white vinegar
1 tablespoon worcestershire sauce (use a vegan version of the sauce to make this vegetarian)
1/2 cup breadcrumbs
2 eggs
1/2 medium (5 oz) yellow onion
3 baby kosher dill pickles
1/4 cup chopped dill
2 tablespoons white vinegar or white balsamic vinegar
1 tablespoon mayonnaise
1/2 teaspoon sugar
1/2 teaspoon Diamond Crystal kosher salt
8 slices white cheddar
8 burger buns
d54aedb9dfe06aece803d9ba4b5ef816c1f8d87f.instructions:
Grate the zucchini into a lint-free towel then crumble in the tofu. Season with 1 teaspoon salt and mix. Let drain for 10 minutes.
To a small pot, add the 2 sliced scallions, 3 grated garlic cloves, 2 tablespoons of tomato paste, 1/4 cup of soy sauce, 2 tablespoons of vinegar, and 1 tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce. Mix until you have a thick paste, then simmer for 2-3 minutes, until it’s a dark brown color. Add this to a medium bowl. Add 1/2 cup of breadcrumbs and 2 eggs and mix to combine..
Squeeze out any excess liquid from the tofu and zucchini, then add them to the breadcrumb mixture and mix until combined.
Using damp hands, scoop out heaping 1/3-cup portions of the mixture and form 8 patties. Place them on a greased or lined half sheet pan and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 450°F.
For the creamy dill pickle slaw, thinly slice 1/2 of a yellow onion and 3 dill pickles, and roughly chop 1/4 cup of dill. In a large bowl, whisk together 2 tablespoons of white vinegar, 1 tablespoon of mayonnaise, 1/2 teaspoon of sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon of salt. Add the onions, pickles, and dill. Give everything a big toss and set aside.
Bake the burger patties at 450°F for 18-22 minutes, then flip them. Top each burger with a slice of cheddar cheese then bake for another 10 minutes, or until the cheese is melted.
To serve, add a burger to a bun, a little ketchup if you're into that, then pile on a big handful of the pickle slaw. Enjoy!
d54aedb9dfe06aece803d9ba4b5ef816c1f8d87f.nutrition:
Calories: 286 kcal
Protein: 13 g
Carbs: 31 g
Fat: 12 g
Serving size: 1 burger

ef2d0a06811ef2851722123628123c78fc1e09e0.title: Sweet Pickled Tomato Skins
ef2d0a06811ef2851722123628123c78fc1e09e0.text: Anything you use pickled red onions on, you can also use pickled tomato skins on! These taste like hot honey pizza in a bite (don't knock it until you try it), and are a salty, tangy, sweet pop of flavor that works on nearly everything savory. If you have tomato skins leftover from making sauce or storing your tomatoes, this is my favorite way to use them.
ef2d0a06811ef2851722123628123c78fc1e09e0.author: Justine Doiron
ef2d0a06811ef2851722123628123c78fc1e09e0.ingredients:
2-3 cups tomato skins (see how to shock your tomatoes in the Note)
5-6 large basil leaves
1 cup water
1 cup white balsamic vinegar
1 tablespoon Diamond Crystal kosher salt
1 tablespoon granulated sugar
ef2d0a06811ef2851722123628123c78fc1e09e0.instructions:
Lightly pat 2-3 cups of tomato skins dry and transfer them to a large jar. Add 5-6 basil leaves.
Add 1 cup of water, 1 cup of white balsamic vinegar, 1 tablespoon of salt, and 1 tablespoon of sugar to a small pot. Bring this to a gentle simmer and stir so the salt and sugar dissolve. Turn off the heat and stir until the mixture is no longer simmering.
Carefully pour this into the jar over the skins, pushing them down so they are fully submerged. Let this cool at room temperature for 45 minutes. Then put on the lid of the jar and store in the fridge.
These will be ready to eat in 2 hours, but at their peak flavor around 12 hours. They will be good for up to two weeks!
ef2d0a06811ef2851722123628123c78fc1e09e0.nutrition:
Calories: 14 kcal
Carbs: 4 g
Serving size: 2 tablespoons

765924057ca5704c9b5d7687ad330a701e6dbfa6.title: Blackberry Ginger Cucumber Salad
765924057ca5704c9b5d7687ad330a701e6dbfa6.text: I love a fruit paired with cucumber, because cucumbers in their own way are quite sweet (and also, technically a fruit!). This ginger dressing is sharp and sweet in a way that perfectly balances the cucumbers and berries, making them both the perfect level of refreshing and sweet. I always say fruit salads need more *umph* - and I like to think this recipe does just that. (Also, if you don't have berries, any kind of summer fruit is pretty great in this!).
765924057ca5704c9b5d7687ad330a701e6dbfa6.author: Justine Doiron
765924057ca5704c9b5d7687ad330a701e6dbfa6.ingredients:
1/2 recipe Five Spice Granola Bark (or 2 tablespoons white sesame seeds)
2 large cucumbers
Diamond Crystal kosher salt
1 pound blackberries
1 cup (1 oz) fresh mint
1 cup (1 oz) fresh basil
# For the creamy ginger dressing:
1-inch knob ginger
2 tablespoons white miso
3 tablespoons lemon juice
2 tablespoons honey
2 tablespoons olive oil
765924057ca5704c9b5d7687ad330a701e6dbfa6.instructions:
First, prepare the sesame bark according to this recipe. If you are just using 2 tablespoons of sesame seeds, add them to a small pan over medium heat. Toast for 2-4 minutes, until they are fragrant and turning golden. Set aside.
Slice 2 cucumbers lengthwise into quarters. Use the flat side of your knife to smash them, seed-side-down, until they are nicely crushed.
Add the crushed cucumbers to a large strainer or sieve and season them with 1 teaspoon of kosher salt. Mix well and let them sit in the sink or over a bowl to drain.
While the cucumbers are draining, wash and halve 1 pound of blackberries and add them to a large bowl. Tear in 1 cup of basil and 1 cup of mint.
In a small blender, like a bullet or ninja, add 1-inch knob of ginger, 2 tablespoons of white miso, 3 tablespoons of lemon juice, 2 tablespoons of honey, and 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Blend until smooth. Taste and season with salt, but I find it never needs any.
Now that the cucumbers have had time to drain, give them a few more big shakes in the sieve to get out any remaining water. Pat them lightly with a paper towel and add them to the bowl with the blackblerries.
Pour in half of the dressing and mix. Add more dressing as desired, and top with the sesame bark or sesame seeds.
Serve right away!
765924057ca5704c9b5d7687ad330a701e6dbfa6.nutrition:
Calories: 204 kcal
Protein: 4 g
Carbs: 27 g
Fat: 10 g
Serving size: 1.5 cups

00a22a636e3a819f3a42e81a9427e3a500f3b8a8.title: Smoky Tomato Burrata Dip
00a22a636e3a819f3a42e81a9427e3a500f3b8a8.text: It's hard for burrata to be bad, but I think it's exceptionally good when it's creamy mild flavor is used to counter something really intense and bright. Enter scene: this five-minute dip that is savory, smoky, tomatoey and fresh all at once. It's simple, but still a step-up from your average tomato-on-burrata plate, and that's exactly why I love it.
00a22a636e3a819f3a42e81a9427e3a500f3b8a8.author: Justine Doiron
00a22a636e3a819f3a42e81a9427e3a500f3b8a8.ingredients:
8 ounces cherry tomatoes or globe tomatoes
3 garlic cloves
2 sprigs fresh oregano
1 teaspoon smoked paprika
1 teaspoon sweet paprika
1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes (omit if you don’t love heat)
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
Diamond Crystal kosher salt
1 teaspoon white wine vinegar
8 ounces burrata (ideally in two 4-ounce balls)
7-8 fresh basil leaves
Assorted chips, crackers, or bread for serving
00a22a636e3a819f3a42e81a9427e3a500f3b8a8.instructions:
Halve the cherry tomatoes, or thinly slice the globe tomatoes. Add them a heat-safe bowl. Grate in the 3 garlic cloves.
To a medium pan, add 2 sprigs of oregano, 1 teaspoon of smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon of sweet paprika, 1/4 teaspoon of red pepper flakes, and 1/4 cup of extra-virgin olive oil. Place this over medium heat and bring to a simmer for 30-60 seconds, until the oregano is fried and crisp.
Pour this over the tomatoes. Season with 1/2 teaspoon of salt and 1 teaspoon of white wine vinegar. Mix, taste and season as preferred. As you mix, the oregano leaves will fall off the stems, so be sure to remove the stems.
To plate, tear up the burrata and layer it across a large plate. Spoon the tomatoes on top. Tear 7-8 basil leaves over top and serve immediately.
00a22a636e3a819f3a42e81a9427e3a500f3b8a8.nutrition:
Calories: 154 kcal
Protein: 7 g
Carbs: 3 g
Fat: 13 g
Serving size: 2 oz

e54fe081cfa9f0cc35ca9ce92cc0c3d5dc4021b8.title: Tomatillo Beans
e54fe081cfa9f0cc35ca9ce92cc0c3d5dc4021b8.text: These beans are inspired by ceviche, but instead of raw fish, we're swapping in some sustainable (and sustaining!) vegetarian protein with white beans. The beans are tossed in a charred tomatillo sauce, and all you need is avocado on top to have a perfect, plant-filled meal!
e54fe081cfa9f0cc35ca9ce92cc0c3d5dc4021b8.author: Justine Doiron
e54fe081cfa9f0cc35ca9ce92cc0c3d5dc4021b8.ingredients:
4 medium (8 oz) tomatillos (halved)
1 jalapeño pepper
2 teaspoons extra-virgin olive oil
1 large (4 oz) Anaheim or poblano pepper, OR 1/2 green bell pepper, OR 1/2 sweet white onion
2 garlic cloves
1 cup (1 oz) fresh cilantro (loosely packed)
1 tablespoon honey
1 tablespoon fresh lime juice
1 tablespoon soy sauce or tamari
3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1 teaspoon Diamond Crystal kosher salt
1/4 (2 oz) medium red onion
1/2 (2 oz) small cucumber
1 (2 oz) medium tomatillo
3/4 cup (0.5 oz) fresh cilantro (loosely packed)
1/2 teaspoon lime zest
2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
1/2 teaspoon Diamond Crystal kosher salt
2 (14 oz) cans white beans (drained and rinsed)
1 tablespoon white wine vinegar (plus more to taste)
Extra-virgin olive oil (for serving )
Flaky salt (for serving)
1 medium avocado
e54fe081cfa9f0cc35ca9ce92cc0c3d5dc4021b8.instructions:
Halve the 4 tomatillos, halve and deseed the jalapeño. Add them both skin-side up to a quarter sheet pan.
Roast at 450°F for 18-22 minutes, or until the skins are charred and the tomatillos are slightly collapsed.
Let them cool while you add the Anaheim pepper, 2 garlic cloves, 1 cup of cilantro, 1 tablespoon of honey, 1 tablespoon of lime juice, and 1 tablespoon of soy sauce to a food processor.
Gently peel off the skins from the tomatillos and jalapeño, use a spatula to scrape all of the interior into the food processor (some of the tomatillo may have burst and stuck to the pan, which is totally fine, just take it with you).
Process until bright green and chunky. Add 3 tablespoons of olive oil and 1 teaspoon of kosher salt then process again until smooth.
Pour this into a large bowl and add the white beans. Mix and add a tablespoon of vinegar. Taste and season with more salt or vinegar as preferred.
Make the cilantro salad by thinly slicing 1/4 of a red onion, 1/2 of a cucumber, and adding it all to a small bowl. Roughly chop 3/4 cup of cilantro and the tomatillo and add both to the bowl. Give a few tosses and season with 1/2 teaspoon of lime zest, 2 tablespoons of lime juice, and 1/2 teaspoon of kosher salt.
To serve, pile the beans into four bowls. Scoop the salad directly on top. Drizzle with extra-virgin olive oil and sprinkle with flaky salt.
Slice up the avocado and add a quarter to each bowl. Serve immediately!
e54fe081cfa9f0cc35ca9ce92cc0c3d5dc4021b8.nutrition:
Calories: 272 kcal
Protein: 6 g
Carbs: 25 g
Fat: 17 g
Serving size: 1 bowl

7116667d4fb6b15173571af01a5c5d33026c6317.title: Zesty salmon tacos
7116667d4fb6b15173571af01a5c5d33026c6317.text: Bright, zesty salmon tacos served with creamy corn salsa, chipotle cabbage and fresh avocado – a quick 20-minute Jamie Oliver recipe for two!
7116667d4fb6b15173571af01a5c5d33026c6317.author: Jamie Oliver
7116667d4fb6b15173571af01a5c5d33026c6317.ingredients:
1 x 200g tin of sweetcorn
½ a bunch of coriander (15g)
2 limes
80g white cabbage
1 heaped teaspoon chipotle chilli paste
½ a ripe avocado
2 ripe tomatoes (160g)
2 x 130g salmon or trout fillets, skin on, scaled, pin-boned, from sustainable sources
6 small corn tortillas
2 tablespoons soured cream
7116667d4fb6b15173571af01a5c5d33026c6317.instructions:
Tip the corn into a blender with just a splash of juice from the tin, tear in half the coriander, stalks and all, squeeze in the juice of 1 lime and blitz until smooth, then season to perfection. Use a speed peeler, box grater or good knife skills to finely shred the white cabbage, then toss with the chipotle paste.
Finely grate and reserve the zest of the remaining lime. Destone the avocado, then scoop the flesh out of the skin, finely slice, and squeeze over half the remaining lime juice. Finely slice the tomatoes and season with a little sea salt.
Put a large non-stick frying pan on a medium-high heat. Slice each salmon fillet lengthways into 3 equal pieces. Season with salt, pat on the reserved lime zest, then spritz the pan with olive oil and fry the salmon for 2 minutes on each side, or until golden and cooked through, briefly warming the tortillas on top.
To serve, spread a spoonful of the corn salsa over each warm tortilla, then divide up the tomatoes, avo and chipotle cabbage. Sit the golden salmon on top, and finish with the soured cream and remaining coriander leaves. Serve with lime wedges and the rest of the corn salsa, for drizzling over.

6597c063c0e1190ab00a4f5ad692d0c320a963e6.title: Thai hot & sour chicken soup
6597c063c0e1190ab00a4f5ad692d0c320a963e6.text: A vibrant 20-minute Thai hot & sour soup recipe – tender chicken, mushrooms and noodles in a fragrant coconut broth with a chilli oil kick. Yum!
6597c063c0e1190ab00a4f5ad692d0c320a963e6.author: Jamie Oliver
6597c063c0e1190ab00a4f5ad692d0c320a963e6.ingredients:
4cm piece of ginger
600g free-range skinless boneless chicken thighs
300g oyster mushrooms
4 heaped tablespoons Thai red curry paste
1 x 400ml tin of light coconut milk
4 nests of free-range egg noodles (250g total)
180g sugar snap peas
160g frozen edamame beans
4 heaped teaspoons crunchy peanut & sesame chilli oil
1 lime
6597c063c0e1190ab00a4f5ad692d0c320a963e6.instructions:
Put a large shallow casserole pan on a high heat with 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Peel, chop and add the ginger. Dice the chicken into 3cm chunks, season with a pinch of sea salt and black pepper and add to the pan with the mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes, or until golden, stirring regularly. Boil the kettle.
Stir the curry paste into the pan. Pour in the coconut milk and 1 litre of boiling kettle water, then submerge the noodles and simmer on a medium heat for
6 minutes, adding the sugar snaps and frozen edamame for the last 3 minutes.
Stir in half the crunchy peanut and sesame chilli oil, season to perfection, then divide between warm bowls. Drizzle over the remaining chilli oil, to finish, and serve with lime wedges, for squeezing over.

272a85f7355bca716839f94a9f68dc35514baf85.title: Sardine linguine
272a85f7355bca716839f94a9f68dc35514baf85.text: Turn tinned fish into a super-tasty meal with Jamie’s 20-minute sardine linguine – easy, delicious and served with a fresh, crunchy fennel salad.
272a85f7355bca716839f94a9f68dc35514baf85.author: Jamie Oliver
272a85f7355bca716839f94a9f68dc35514baf85.ingredients:
1 onion (160g)
1 clove of garlic
1 x 120g tin of sardines in olive oil, from sustainable sources
½ a bunch of flat-leaf parsley (15g)
½–1 fresh red chilli
1 tablespoon baby capers in brine
150g dried linguine
1 small bulb of fennel (160g)
1 lemon
2 tablespoons pine nuts
272a85f7355bca716839f94a9f68dc35514baf85.instructions:
Boil the kettle. Peel and coarsely grate the onion, peel and finely grate the garlic, then place it all in a frying pan on a medium-high heat with the oil from the sardine tin. Finely slice and add the parsley stalks, reserving the leaves. Finely slice the chilli and add half to the pan, along with the capers, a splash of their brine and 100ml of water. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring regularly.
Meanwhile, cook the linguine in a pan of boiling salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet instructions, until al dente. Use a speed peeler to finely slice the fennel, reserving any herby tops. Toss with the parsley leaves and the remaining sliced chilli, and finely grate over the lemon zest.
Break the sardines into the onion pan and add the pine nuts. Cook on a low heat, stirring regularly and giving it some love, until the pasta is ready.
Squeeze half the lemon juice over the sardines, then use tongs to drag across the linguine. Feed it with enough cooking water to create a silky sauce, cooking for another 2 minutes, or until the pasta is perfect. Season to perfection, then serve with the salad, and lemon wedges, for squeezing over.

ed0be33e37876b07f4d58fa4ea5ba7142143b05f.title: Goat's cheese & bramble salad
ed0be33e37876b07f4d58fa4ea5ba7142143b05f.text: Warm goat’s cheese on sourdough toasts over a fresh berry, green bean and hazelnut salad – a totally delicious 20-minute recipe for two!
ed0be33e37876b07f4d58fa4ea5ba7142143b05f.author: Jamie Oliver
ed0be33e37876b07f4d58fa4ea5ba7142143b05f.ingredients:
30g blanched hazelnuts
160g fine green beans
150g blackberries & raspberries
2 teaspoons Dijon mustard
100g sourdough French baguette
60g goat’s cheese
1 red onion (160g)
1 round lettuce
½ a bunch of tarragon (10g)
ed0be33e37876b07f4d58fa4ea5ba7142143b05f.instructions:
Turn the grill on to medium. Put a large non-stick pan on a medium-high heat and toast the hazelnuts as it heats up, tossing until golden. Remove to a pestle and mortar and roughly smash. Trim and char the green beans, tossing regularly.
Meanwhile, to make the dressing, use a fork to mush up half the berries in a large bowl. Mix with the mustard, 1 tablespoon of red wine vinegar and 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil, then season to perfection.
Slice the bread into 4 pieces at an angle and place on a roasting tray. Slice the goat’s cheese into 8 rounds, divide between the bread, then add ½ a teaspoon of dressing to each. Spritz with olive oil and grill for 5 minutes, or until golden.
Once the green beans have started to soften, tip them straight into the bowl of dressing. Peel and very finely slice the onion and add to the hot pan with a pinch of salt, a spritz of oil and a good splash of water. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring regularly, then add 1 tablespoon of vinegar and let the onions soften.
Trim the base of the lettuce, click the leaves apart, then wash and spin dry. Pick the tarragon leaves. Add it all to the bowl of dressing with the softened onions and gently toss together. Scatter over the smashed hazelnuts and the remaining berries. Sit the toasts proudly on top, divvy up and enjoy!

a4293bb7dbecbdde461de098c063933d9d9d6264.title: Pizza fritte duo
a4293bb7dbecbdde461de098c063933d9d9d6264.text: Try Jamie’s 20-minute pizza fritte duo – crispy, puffed dough topped with broad bean and mozzarella, plus a fresh garlic tomato sauce. Delicious!
a4293bb7dbecbdde461de098c063933d9d9d6264.author: Jamie Oliver
a4293bb7dbecbdde461de098c063933d9d9d6264.ingredients:
150g self-raising flour, plus extra for dusting
80g frozen broad beans
1 ripe tomato (100g)
½ a small clove of garlic
½ teaspoon dried oregano
½ a fresh red chilli
1 sprig of basil
½ a lemon
½ x 125g ball of mozzarella cheese
20g pecorino or Parmesan cheese
a4293bb7dbecbdde461de098c063933d9d9d6264.instructions:
Boil the kettle. Put the flour into a bowl with a pinch of sea salt and make a well in the middle, then gradually add 90ml of water, stirring constantly with a fork until it becomes too hard to mix. Get your clean hands in there and bring together as a dough, then divide into 4 balls and leave to rest for a moment.
Cook the broad beans in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain. Meanwhile, halve the tomato and finely grate cut side down into a bowl so you get a slurry, discarding the skin. Peel and finely grate in the garlic, then mix with the oregano and 1 teaspoon of extra virgin olive oil, and season to perfection with salt and black pepper. Finely chop the chilli. Pick the basil.
Place the broad beans in a small food processor or blender with 1 teaspoon of extra virgin olive oil. Finely grate and reserve the lemon zest, then squeeze the juice into the processor. Blitz to a coarse paste, loosening with a splash of water, if needed, then season to perfection.
Put a large frying pan on a medium-high heat with ½cm of olive oil and let it get hot while you roll out each dough ball on a clean floured surface into a 14cm round. Working two at a time, gently place the dough rounds in the oil and cook for 3 minutes, or until golden, puffed up and cooked through, turning halfway, then drain on kitchen paper and move to your plates.
Top two fritte with the broad bean smash, torn mozzarella, reserved lemon zest, chilli and basil leaves. Spoon the tomato sauce over the other two, grating over the Parmesan. Finish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, if you like.

9fd0589e610dcc69b4233a46329a1bae5346538d.title: Pressure cooker Bolognese
9fd0589e610dcc69b4233a46329a1bae5346538d.text: Make Jamie's pressure cooker Bolognese in just 20 minutes! Rich beef, lentils, red wine and porcini – beautiful slow-cooked flavour in minutes.
9fd0589e610dcc69b4233a46329a1bae5346538d.author: Jamie Oliver
9fd0589e610dcc69b4233a46329a1bae5346538d.ingredients:
250g higher-welfare beef mince
250g fresh or frozen chopped mixed onion, carrot & celery
optional: 10g dried porcini mushrooms
4 sprigs of rosemary
2 cloves of garlic
4 tablespoons double concentrate tomato purée
125ml red wine
1 x 400g tin of lentils
300g dried penne pasta
30g Parmesan cheese
9fd0589e610dcc69b4233a46329a1bae5346538d.instructions:
Put the pressure cooker on a high heat with 2 tablespoons of olive oil, the mince and chopped mixed veg, and crumble in the porcini, if using, stirring regularly. Pick and finely chop the rosemary, peel and finely chop the garlic, and stir into the pan with the tomato purée, wine, lentils, juice and all, along with ½ a tin’s worth of water and a pinch of sea salt and black pepper. Clamp the lid on and, as soon as the steam starts to release, cook for 10 minutes on medium.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in a pan of boiling salted water according to the packet instructions, then drain, reserving a mugful of starchy cooking water.
Release the steam from the pressure cooker and, once ready, carefully remove the lid. Mash the Bolognese with a potato masher, loosening with a splash of reserved cooking water, if needed, then season to perfection and toss with the drained pasta. Pour on to a platter, finely grate over the Parmesan, and drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil to finish, if you like.

a241250d9003074e7f6ad84cceb1b88b64d7587c.title: Pierogi
a241250d9003074e7f6ad84cceb1b88b64d7587c.text: A quick and easy 20-minute cheese and potato pierogi recipe – serve with steamed greens, soured cream and herbs for a winning weeknight dinner!
a241250d9003074e7f6ad84cceb1b88b64d7587c.author: Jamie Oliver
a241250d9003074e7f6ad84cceb1b88b64d7587c.ingredients:
100g self-raising flour
1 x 300g tin of peeled new potatoes
60g Cheddar cheese
1 bunch of chives (20g)
½ a head of broccoli (160g)
160g rainbow chard
175g soured cream
4 olives, stone in
30g shelled walnut halves
½ a bunch of dill (10g)
a241250d9003074e7f6ad84cceb1b88b64d7587c.instructions:
Boil the kettle. Mix the flour, a small pinch of sea salt and 50ml of the tinned potato water until you have a dough, then knead for a couple of minutes, or until smooth. Divide into 4, roll into balls, cover, and set aside for a moment.
Drain the potatoes, place in a bowl, grate in the cheese, finely chop and add most of the chives, then scrunch well and season to perfection. Working quickly, on a clean floured surface, roll out the dough balls into rounds just under ½cm thick. Divide the potato filling between them, lightly brush the exposed dough with water, then bring the edges up and over the filling, pressing to seal.
Put a large deep pan on a medium-high heat and half fill with boiling salted water. Chop the broccoli into small florets, discarding the stalk, place in a colander, and tear in the chard. Lower the pierogi into the water, sit the colander on top, cover, and cook for 6 minutes, or until everything is cooked through.
Meanwhile, mix most of the remaining chives with the soured cream, season to perfection and divide between plates. Move the steamed greens to your board, tear over the olives, discarding the stones, add the walnuts and most of the dill, then finely chop, mixing as you go. Toss with 1 teaspoon of red wine vinegar and 1 tablespoon of extra virgin olive oil, season to perfection and divide up.
Lift out the pierogi and sit them on top of the veg, sprinkle over the reserved dill, and finish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, if you like.

fa62aca5c330a9a932e5a97cbf1fdf16c8ef6141.title: Chicken & sausage stew
fa62aca5c330a9a932e5a97cbf1fdf16c8ef6141.text: An easy 20-minute chicken, sausage & borlotti bean stew with tomatoes, broccoli, garlic and a crispy rosemary bread topping. Seriously tasty!
fa62aca5c330a9a932e5a97cbf1fdf16c8ef6141.author: Jamie Oliver
fa62aca5c330a9a932e5a97cbf1fdf16c8ef6141.ingredients:
1 x 150g free-range skinless chicken breast
2 rashers of smoked higher-welfare pancetta
2 higher-welfare sausages (130g)
1 x 400g tin of cherry tomatoes
1 x 400g tin of borlotti beans
160g purple sprouting broccoli
½ a bunch of rosemary (10g)
2 cloves of garlic
1 lemon
2 large slices of sourdough bread (100g each)
fa62aca5c330a9a932e5a97cbf1fdf16c8ef6141.instructions:
Turn the grill on to high. Put a large shallow casserole pan on a high heat with1 tablespoon of olive oil. Adding it all to the pan as you go, chop the chicken into 6 equal pieces and halve the pancetta and sausages. Cook for 9 minutes, stirring occasionally, or until golden.
Tip the tomatoes into the pan, then add the beans, juice and all, and 1 tablespoon of red wine vinegar. Bring to the boil, then trim and add the broccoli, halving any thicker stalks lengthways. Leave to simmer while you make the topping.
Strip the rosemary into a pestle and mortar and pound with a small pinch of sea salt, then peel and bash in the garlic. Finely grate in the lemon zest, then muddle in half the juice and 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil, and season to perfection. Tear the bread into bite-size chunks and scrunch with the mixture.
Season the stew to perfection, then scatter the herby dressed bread over the top. Carefully transfer to the grill for 5 minutes, or until golden, bubbling and cooked through, then serve with lemon wedges, for squeezing over.

70c480a17e5ccd1fbc11afdefc58596843a18b0b.title: Tomato & feta lentils
70c480a17e5ccd1fbc11afdefc58596843a18b0b.text: An easy 20-minute tomato & feta lentil dish – rich roasted pepper lentils topped with feta, herbs and pistachios. Served with warm flatbreads.
70c480a17e5ccd1fbc11afdefc58596843a18b0b.author: Jamie Oliver
70c480a17e5ccd1fbc11afdefc58596843a18b0b.ingredients:
4 cloves of garlic
1 fresh red chilli
500g ripe tomatoes
1 x 460g jar of roasted red peppers
½ a pomegranate
30g shelled unsalted pistachio nuts
1 bunch of dill (20g)
4 flatbreads
2 x 400g tins of lentils
100g feta cheese
70c480a17e5ccd1fbc11afdefc58596843a18b0b.instructions:
Peel the garlic and finely slice with the chilli, then place in a shallow casserole pan on a medium-high heat with 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Cook until soft but not coloured, stirring regularly. Chop and add the tomatoes. Tip the peppers into a blender, juice and all, blitz until smooth, then pour into the pan. Cook for 8 minutes, or until thickened, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, hold the pomegranate half cut side down in your palm and bash the back of it so the seeds tumble out into a bowl. Finely chop the pistachios. Pick and chop the dill. Warm the flatbreads.
Drain the lentils and add to the pan, along with ½ a tablespoon of red wine vinegar. Simmer for a final 5 minutes, then stir through half the pomegranate seeds and half the chopped dill, and season to perfection.
Scatter over the pistachios and the remaining pomegranate seeds, crumble over the feta, and sprinkle over the remaining dill. Serve with the warm flatbreads.

718671f9686032ba94b50e37a9e0684556ff17a5.title: Bread & borlotti bean soup
718671f9686032ba94b50e37a9e0684556ff17a5.text: An easy 20-minute bread & borlotti bean soup. Loaded with tomatoes, melted mozzarella and crispy sage it's a real treat for the taste buds.
718671f9686032ba94b50e37a9e0684556ff17a5.author: Jamie Oliver
718671f9686032ba94b50e37a9e0684556ff17a5.ingredients:
1 bunch of sage (20g)
500g frozen chopped mixed onion, carrot & celery
2 cloves of garlic
300g stale sourdough bread
2 x 400g tins of plum tomatoes
2 x 400g tins of borlotti beans
700ml organic veg or chicken stock
25g Parmesan cheese
1 x 125g ball of mozzarella cheese
718671f9686032ba94b50e37a9e0684556ff17a5.instructions:
Turn the grill on to high. Put a large shallow ovenproof casserole pan on a medium-high heat with 4 tablespoons of olive oil and pick in the sage leaves. Fry until crispy, then remove to a plate, leaving the fragrant oil behind.
Add the chopped mixed veg to the pan, then peel, finely slice and add the garlic, along with a splash of water. Cover and cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Chop the bread into 3cm chunks. Turn the heat up to high and pour the tomatoes into the pan, breaking them up with your spoon, then go in with the beans, juice and all, the stock and the bread. Stir and mash it up together for
5 minutes, then finely grate in the Parmesan and season to perfection.
Tear over the mozzarella, then carefully transfer to under the grill for 5 minutes, or until the cheese has melted and the soup is bubbling away. Sprinkle over the crispy sage, and finish with a few drips of extra virgin olive oil, if you like.

b88ab4c3d93fb92a680fde9254965c4b7eec5bd9.title: Pizza pepperoni
b88ab4c3d93fb92a680fde9254965c4b7eec5bd9.text: Pepperoni pizza is always a winner at a pizza party. It's a great classic and here is my version of a pepperoni pizza. Pick up a hot pepperoni if you want a spicy little pizza.
b88ab4c3d93fb92a680fde9254965c4b7eec5bd9.author: Andy
b88ab4c3d93fb92a680fde9254965c4b7eec5bd9.ingredients:
3 dough balls
1 can San Marzano tomatoes
250g mozzarella
salt, to taste
24 slices pepperoni
extra virgin olive oil (EVOO)
1 cup semolina flour
b88ab4c3d93fb92a680fde9254965c4b7eec5bd9.instructions:
Preheat your pizza oven to 480°C (900°F). If using your domestic oven, place the pizza steel inside and preheat it to the highest possible temperature.
For the tomato sauce, add the canned tomatoes, a few torn basil leaves, and a pinch of salt to a bowl. Using clean hands, crush the tomatoes for 1-2 minutes, or until most of the large lumps are gone.
Slice the mozzarella into pieces roughly the size of your index finger.
To stretch the dough, cut it from the box it was proved in using a dough cutter on every side. Remove the dough from the container and then place it top side down into the bowl of semolina. Working away from yourself, press the dough outwards, leaving a 2cm (about 0.8 inch) rim around the edge. Turn the dough 90° and repeat. Carefully remove the dough from the semolina and place it over the backs of your hands, stretching it out slightly, then place onto a lightly floured bench.
To assemble the pizza, lay down 1-2 spoons of the tomato sauce in the centre of the dough, Use the back of a spoon to spread the tomato sauce evenly leaving a 2cm (about 0.8 inch) gap around the edge Add the pepperoni, then mozzarella cheese, and drizzle with extra-virgin olive oil.
Carefully pick up the pizza with a pizza peel, ensuring it's the shape and size you want, then place it into your pizza oven. If using a pizza oven, after 45-50 seconds, or when the crust closest to the heat source starts to colour, begin turning the pizza. It should cook in about 90 seconds.
If cooking in a domestic oven with a pizza steel, place the pizza in the centre of the steel and close the door quickly. There's less need to turn the pizza as it should have a more even heat distribution, but it will take longer to cook, around 5-6 minutes.

82a7503229205352cf1b2c7d1b919489232fc62c.title: Brussels Sprout Fried Eggs with Lemon and Parmesan
82a7503229205352cf1b2c7d1b919489232fc62c.text: Brussels sprouts are one of my favorite fall vegetables, and this quick and simple method is one of my best ways to turn them into a filling lunch or dinner. Frying eggs directly on top of brussels sprouts keeps them all frizzled on the edges, plus some fried lemon, toasted sage and crisp rosemary makes me feel like I'm treating myself to a proper fall meal - even though it all happens in under 30 minutes.
82a7503229205352cf1b2c7d1b919489232fc62c.author: Justine Doiron
82a7503229205352cf1b2c7d1b919489232fc62c.ingredients:
8 ounces Brussels sprouts
1 lemon (halved)
3 sprigs rosemary
5 sage leaves
3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes
1/2 teaspoon Diamond Crystal kosher salt
Freshly cracked black pepper
4 large eggs
1 ounce parmesan (for topping)
82a7503229205352cf1b2c7d1b919489232fc62c.instructions:
Thinly slice 8 ounces of brussels sprouts (around 2 cups). Halve the lemon. Cut one half into wedges and set aside. Peel the other half and finely chop up the pulp, removing any seeds.
Finely chop the leaves of 3 sprigs of rosemary and 5 sage leaves.
Put a large sauté pan with a tight fitted lid over medium heat. Add in 3 tablespoons of olive oil.
Add the chopped lemon, herbs, 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 2-3 minutes, or until you start to see the lemon lightly char and the herbs crisp up. Add in the brussels sprouts.
Cook the sprouts, stirring occasionally, for what feels like too long, 10-12 minutes or until the brussels sprouts are about half the size and beginning to get some browning.
Make four small "divets" in the brussels sprouts and crack an egg into each one. Season the eggs lightly with salt and pepper.
Cover and let the eggs cook for 4-5 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Scoop two eggs onto each plate, taking the sprouts along with them. Grate on some parmesan and serve with the remaining lemon wedges.
